questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
Due to failing health, the owner of a condominium unit in a resort area decided to move in with her sister who lived across the country. The owner, unable to bring herself to permanently part with the unit, orally agreed to rent the unit to a friend for two years. One week after they had shaken hands on the deal, the owner wrote out the essential terms of the rental agreement, except for the identity of the renter, and placed the unsigned document in her files. One month later, the owner sent an unsigned email to her sister telling her to expect the owner by a certain date because her friend, whom she identified by name, was moving into the unit the weekend following that date. She also noted in the email that, if anything should happen to her, the terms of the rental agreement could be found among her papers. Two weeks before she was to move, the owner died. When the friend attempted to move into the unit, the personal representative of the owner's estate blocked his attempt.
The friend brought an action to compel the personal representative to permit him to occupy the condominium unit. The personal representative has raised the statute of frauds as a defense.
Which of the following best supports the personal representative's defense?

choices.A: None of the writings, standing alone, contained all the essential elements of the rental agreement.
choices.B: None of the writings were prepared contemporaneously with the rental agreement.
choices.C: None of the writings were signed by the owner.
choices.D: None of the writings were transmitted to the friend.

questions.explanation:
Contracts subject to statute of frauds
  • Marriage – promise in consideration of marriage
  • Year – contract cannot be completed within one year
  • Land – sale or other transfer of real property
  • Executor – promise to pay estate's debt from executor's personal funds
  • Goods – sale of goods for $500 or more
  • Suretyship – promise to pay another's debt
Mnemonic: MY LEGS

Contracts that fall within the statute of frauds (see table above), including a sale or other transfer of real property (e.g., lease) for more than one year, are unenforceable unless evidenced by a writing. The writing need not be written at the time the promise is made or delivered. However, the writing must:

  • be signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought and
  • contain the essential elementsEssential elements of a contract under the statute of frauds include the identity of the parties, subject matter, price, and material terms of performance. (必要条款) of the deal.

The essential elements may be in more than one writing if one of the writings references the other writing(s).

Here, all essential terms except the identity of the renter were in the document the owner placed in her files, and the renter's name was in the email the owner sent to her sister. And because that email referenced the document in the owner's files, both can be considered together in determining whether the statute of frauds has been satisfied (Choice A). But neither document was signed by the owner. Therefore, this is the best argument that supports the personal representative's statute of frauds defense.

(Choices B & D) To satisfy the statute of frauds, a writing need not be contemporaneous with the agreement or possessed by the party seeking to enforce the writing. Therefore, the timing of when the writings were prepared and the fact that the owner did not transmit them to the friend are irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts that fall within the statute of frauds must be in a writing that (1) is signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought and (2) contains the essential elements of the deal. The essential elements may be in more than one writing if one of the writings references the other writing(s).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 178 (listing the classes of contracts subject to the statute of frauds and the requirements for enforcement).
questions.zh-question: 由于健康状况不佳，一位在度假区拥有公寓单元（condominium unit）的业主决定搬去和住在全国另一端的姐姐一起住。业主不忍心永久放弃该单元，口头同意将该单元租给一位朋友两年。在他们达成口头协议并握手一周后，业主写下了租赁协议（rental agreement）的基本条款，但没有写明承租人的身份，并将这份未签名的文件放入她的档案中。一个月后，业主给她的姐姐发了一封未签名的电子邮件，告诉她在一个特定日期前等她，因为她的朋友（她指明了姓名）将在那个日期后的周末搬入该单元。她还在邮件中提到，如果她发生任何意外，租赁协议的条款可以在她的文件中找到。在她搬家前两周，业主去世了。当朋友试图搬入该单元时，业主遗产的个人代表（personal representative）阻止了他。朋友提起诉讼，要求个人代表允许他占用该公寓单元。个人代表提出了欺诈法（statute of frauds）作为抗辩。以下哪项最能支持个人代表的抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 没有任何一份书面文件，单独来看，包含了租赁协议的所有基本要素。
zh-choices.B: 没有任何一份书面文件是与租赁协议同时准备的。
zh-choices.C: 没有任何一份书面文件是由业主签署的。
zh-choices.D: 没有任何一份书面文件被传送给朋友。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Statute of frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：租期超过一年的不动产租赁（lease）落入法规上的书面要求（statute of frauds）后，能不能靠两份互相指向的书面材料补齐要件，以及是否必须有被追责一方签名（signed by the party to be charged）。

三秒认题路径：

租两年 → 不动产租赁 → 进SOF → 需书面+签名 → 选无签名

核心法律规则

落入法规上的书面要求（statute of frauds）的合同，像这里的不动产租赁（lease）超过一年，原则上必须有书面证据。考试上最关键的是：书面要包含必要条款（essential elements），而且要由被追责一方签名，意思就是将来拿来起诉的人，得能拿着这份书面去卡住对方。

多个书面可以合并看，但前提是其中一份能指向另一份，这样才算一套。这里真正卡死的是：材料虽然能拼出交易内容，但没有任何一份是屋主签的，所以对方还是能用statute of frauds挡掉强制履行。

核心判例： 题目没有要求特定判例名；按通用规则记：书面内容够不够和有没有签名是两道不同关卡，第二道不过就输。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 statute of frauds 题？
YES：
两年租约 + 不动产
→ 落入 SOF
→
看书面是否够
必要条款可拼接
→
再问：有无被追责一方签名？
NO：
没有 owner 签名 → 直接卡死 → 不能强制履行
题内诱饵：
两份书面能互相指向
≠ 自动合格
→
真正缺口是签名，不是时间或送达

考点陷阱

你可能会想：两份材料加起来已经写清楚了房子、租期和承租人，应该够了。

但考试真正问的是：这些内容能不能被拿来对抗屋主一方，关键还差不差签名（signature）。本题看的是「能不能满足书面法定要求」，不是「信息有没有被写下来」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干两份材料虽然能拼出交易内容，但都没有屋主签名；签名缺失正好击中 statute of frauds 的硬门槛。

❌ 概念混淆 | 内容拼接误判

✕ A: 把“分散在两份书面里”误当成“内容不全”。

❌ 事实误判 | 同时制作误判

✕ B: 抓着 contemporaneously 不放，但书面不必同日完成。

❌ 法律适用 | 送达对象误判

✕ D: 误以为必须交给承租人才算数，发送对象不是门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否进 SOF，再查书面要件，最后只盯签名这一刀能不能把对方挡住。

考场速记

记住一句：SOF 看两件事，内容够不够，签名在不在。多份书面可以互相补，但没有被追责一方签名，还是过不了。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
Before putting her home up for sale, a homeowner painted the living room ceiling to conceal major water damage caused by a leaking roof that had not yet been repaired. On the first day the home was offered for sale, the homeowner gave a buyer a personal tour. The homeowner made no statements at all regarding the water damage or the roof. Without discovering the water damage or the leaking roof and without consulting a lawyer, the buyer immediately agreed in writing to buy the home for $200,000. Before the closing date, the buyer discovered the water damage and the leaking roof. The cost of repair was estimated at $22,000. The buyer has refused to go through with the purchase.
If the homeowner sues the buyer for breach of contract, is the homeowner likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because no contract was formed since the buyer did not have a real opportunity to understand the essential terms of the contract.
choices.B: No, because the homeowner concealed evidence of the water damage and of the leaking roof.
choices.C: Yes, because the buyer acted unreasonably by failing to employ an inspector to conduct an independent inspection of the home.
choices.D: Yes, because the homeowner made no affirmative statements of fact about the water damage or the leaking roof.

questions.explanation:
When reliance on misrepresentation is justified
Fact
(almost always justified) 		If untrue assertion is presented as fact, party's reliance justified unless:
  • assertion is patently false or
  • party knows assertion is false
Opinion*
(rarely justified) 		If untrue assertion is presented as opinion, party's reliance justified only if:
  • facts as speaker understands them are consistent with or justify opinion
  • relationship of trust & confidence exists
  • party reasonably believes speaker has special expertise or
  • party is particularly susceptible to type of misrepresentation involved
*A statement of opinion is also a statement of fact—and can therefore be a misrepresentation—because it states that a person has a particular state of mind.

Misrepresentation is an untrue assertion of fact made by words or conduct (eg, concealment—an act intended to prevent discovery of facts). When this occurs, a contract is voidable by the adversely affected party if:

  • the misrepresentation was fraudulent (ie, made knowingly or recklessly with intent to induce the other party's assent to the contract) OR material (ie, likely to induce a reasonable person's assent)
  • the misrepresentation induced assent to the contract and
  • the adversely affected party justifiably relied on the misrepresentation.

Here, the homeowner painted the living room ceiling to conceal water damage and a leaking roof. As a result of this fraudulent misrepresentation, the buyer decided to purchase the home. And since the homeowner never mentioned the water damage or roof during the personal tour, the buyer justifiably relied on the misrepresentation. Therefore, the buyer can avoid the contract and the homeowner is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice A) No contract is formed (ie, the apparent contract is void) if a fraudulent misrepresentation prevents a party from knowing the character or essential terms of the transaction and the party did not have a reasonable opportunity to understand those terms. But there is no evidence that the buyer did not understand the essential terms of the contract here.

(Choice C) A party's reliance on a misrepresentation is justified unless the misrepresentation is patently false (eg, if the water damage was visible) or the party knows it to be false. Therefore, the buyer's failure to inspect the home does not bar relief.

(Choice D) An affirmative statement is not required for a misrepresentation to occur. Affirmative conduct intended to prevent another from discovering a fact (eg, concealment) also qualifies as a misrepresentation.

📌 Educational Objective

A contract is voidable for misrepresentation if (1) the misrepresentation was fraudulent or material, (2) it induced assent to the contract, and (3) the adversely affected party justifiably relied on the misrepresentation.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when misrepresentation makes a contract voidable).
questions.zh-question:
在将其房屋挂牌出售前，一位房主粉刷了客厅天花板，以掩盖因屋顶漏水（尚未修复）造成的严重水渍。在房屋开始出售的第一天，房主亲自带领一位买家参观了房屋。房主完全没有提及水渍或屋顶漏水的情况。买家在没有发现水渍或屋顶漏水，也未咨询律师的情况下，立即书面同意以20万美元的价格购买该房屋。在交割日之前，买家发现了水渍和屋顶漏水问题。维修费用估计为22,000美元。买家已拒绝继续完成此项购买。

如果房主以违约为由起诉买家，房主是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为合同并未成立，原因是买家没有真正的机会去理解合同的基本条款。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为房主隐瞒了水渍和屋顶漏水的证据。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为买家未能聘请验房师对房屋进行独立检查，其行为不合理。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为房主没有就水渍或屋顶漏水问题作出任何肯定的事实陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖家用 隐瞒/遮掩（concealment） 把房屋缺陷藏起来，构成 虚假陈述（misrepresentation），所以买家可以撤销合同，卖家不能强迫履行。

三秒认题路径：

涂墙遮掩 → 故意隐瞒 → 误导买受人 → 可撤销 → 卖家败诉

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

虚假陈述（misrepresentation） 不一定要靠明说；故意隐瞒（concealment） 也是。考场意思：只要一方用动作把事实藏起来，让对方在误解中签约，就可能让合同变成 可撤销（voidable）。

这里要看三件事：陈述或遮掩是 重大（material） 或 欺诈性（fraudulent），它诱使对方同意，而且受害方 正当依赖（justifiably relied） 了。考场意思：不是看卖家有没有“开口骗人”，而是看他有没有把关键坏消息藏住。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 — 只要欺诈性或重大虚假陈述诱使对方同意，合同就可被受害方撤销。

思维导图

卖家只是“没说”，还是“故意藏”？
①先看行为：涂墙遮掩（concealment） 不是沉默，而是主动把缺陷藏起来。
②再看作用：遮掩的是 水损和漏屋顶，这是会直接影响买房决定的关键信息。
③法律关卡：这就落进 虚假陈述（misrepresentation），不要求一定有口头假话。
卡死点：买家日后能救济，合同可撤销；所以卖家不能靠“我一句都没说”脱身。
④结论：选 B，因为题干事实已经把“隐瞒”钉死了。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖家根本没明说，所以不算骗人。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有用 concealment 把事实藏住，让买家在误解里签字。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

买家后来发现缺陷，不代表他当初没被误导；卖家把墙刷一遍，已经足够构成可撤销的欺诈性隐瞒。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 painted the living room ceiling to conceal water damage，这是故意隐瞒缺陷，直接构成 misrepresentation，买家可撤销合同。

❌ 概念混淆 | 形成无效误判

✕ A: 把撤销合同误当成“根本没成立”。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽视隐瞒行为

✕ C: 盯着 independent inspection，错把买家没验房当成放弃救济。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看明说漏判

✕ D: 误以为必须有明示假话，忽略了 concealment 也算。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有故意藏事实”，再问“这会不会让合同可撤销”，不要被“卖家没开口”带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：不只假话会骗，遮掩事实也会骗。看到 concealment、material、voidable，先想“买家能不能撤”，再想“卖家能不能赢”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify fraudulent concealment permitting contract avoidance

keywords.text: painted the living room ceiling to conceal

reason.en: Conduct intended to hide a material defect constitutes a misrepresentation.
reason.zh: 旨在隐藏重大缺陷的行为构成虚假陈述。

reason.en: The severity of the concealed defect supports materiality.
reason.zh: 被隐瞒缺陷的严重程度支持其重大性。

reason.en: The roof problem remained an existing defect when the contract was made.
reason.zh: 订立合同时屋顶问题仍是现实存在的缺陷。

reason.en: Silence does not prevent prior active concealment from being a misrepresentation.
reason.zh: 沉默不妨碍先前的积极隐瞒构成虚假陈述。

reason.en: This fact does not defeat justified reliance on the concealed condition.
reason.zh: 该事实不否定买方对隐瞒状况的正当信赖。

reason.en: The buyer discovered the fraud before performance and could avoid the contract.
reason.zh: 买方在履行前发现欺诈，因此可以撤销合同。

keywords.text: refused to go through with the purchase

reason.en: The buyer seeks to avoid a contract induced by fraudulent concealment.
reason.zh: 买方试图撤销因欺诈性隐瞒而订立的合同。

reason.en: Fraudulent concealment generally makes the contract voidable, not nonexistent.
reason.zh: 欺诈性隐瞒通常使合同可撤销，而非自始未成立。

label.zh: 交易性质或合同必要条款

reason.en: Nothing indicates that the buyer misunderstood the transaction or its essential terms.
reason.zh: 没有事实表明买方误解了交易性质或必要条款。

reason.en: The homeowner's deliberate concealment is a fraudulent misrepresentation by conduct.
reason.zh: 房主的故意隐瞒属于以行为作出的欺诈性虚假陈述。

reason.en: The hidden damage materially affected the value and condition of the home.
reason.zh: 被隐藏的损害重大影响房屋价值和状况。

reason.en: The ongoing leak confirms that the concealed condition was substantial.
reason.zh: 持续漏水表明被隐瞒的问题十分重大。

reason.en: A victim ordinarily need not independently investigate a concealed factual representation.
reason.zh: 受害方通常无须独立调查被隐瞒的事实性陈述。

reason.en: Failure to inspect does not bar relief when the defect was deliberately concealed.
reason.zh: 缺陷被故意隐藏时，未检查并不阻碍救济。

reason.en: The law does not shift the loss to the buyer merely for omitting an inspection.
reason.zh: 法律不会仅因买方未检查就将损失转嫁给买方。

reason.en: Misrepresentation may arise from concealment by conduct without spoken assertions.
reason.zh: 即使没有口头陈述，以行为隐瞒也可构成虚假陈述。

reason.en: The absence of words does not excuse conduct designed to hide this defect.
reason.zh: 没有言语陈述并不能免除故意隐藏该缺陷的责任。

highlights.text: painted the living room ceiling to conceal major water damage

reason.en: This act constitutes a factual misrepresentation despite the absence of words.
reason.zh: 即使没有言语陈述，该行为仍构成事实虚假陈述。

highlights.text: a leaking roof that had not yet been repaired

reason.en: The unrepaired leak makes the concealed condition material to the purchase.
reason.zh: 未修复的漏水问题使被隐瞒状况对购房决定具有重大性。

highlights.text: The homeowner made no statements at all regarding the water damage or the roof.

reason.en: The absence of an oral assertion does not negate misrepresentation by concealment.
reason.zh: 没有口头陈述并不否定通过隐瞒构成的虚假陈述。

highlights.text: Without discovering the water damage or the leaking roof

reason.en: The buyer assented without knowing the concealed facts, supporting inducement and reliance.
reason.zh: 买方在不知被隐瞒事实的情况下同意交易，支持诱导与信赖要件。

highlights.text: The cost of repair was estimated at $22,000.

reason.en: The substantial repair cost shows that the concealed defect was likely to induce assent.
reason.zh: 高额维修费用表明该隐瞒缺陷很可能影响同意订约。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An elderly widow had one child, an adult son, who lived out-of-state. The widow was in poor health, so she hired a live-in caregiver to tend to her daily needs. Knowing that the widow owned a successful bakery business, the caregiver befriended the widow in order to convince her to sell her business to the caregiver. When the widow later decided to sell the business to her son, the caregiver became upset. She falsely told the widow that there were no other reliable caregivers available in the widow's community. The caregiver then threatened to quit her job and never speak to the widow again unless the widow agreed to sell the business to the caregiver. Although the widow knew that there were other caregivers available, she depended on the caregiver and was terrified of being without her. The widow therefore executed a contract selling the business to the caregiver for less than half its market value.
Shortly thereafter, the widow was placed under the son's guardianship. When the son learned about the contract and the caregiver's threat, he sued to have the contract annulled on the widow's behalf.
On what basis is the son most likely to prevail?

choices.A: Duress.
choices.B: Lack of capacity.
choices.C: Misrepresentation.
choices.D: Undue influence.

questions.explanation:
Undue Influence

A contract is voidablevoidable (可撤销的) for undue influence if a party's assent was the product of unfair or excessive persuasion by someone who dominated or shared a special relationship of trust and confidence with that party. Persuasion is unfair or excessive if it seriously impairs the assenting party's ability to exercise free and competent judgment. The following factors are relevant to making this determination:

  • Susceptibility of the assenting party (eg, elderly, in poor health)
  • Unfairness of the resulting bargain (eg, sale of business for less than half its market value)
  • Unavailability of independent advice (eg, attorney unavailable to discuss sale)

Here, the widow relied on the caregiver to tend to her daily needs (dominant relationship). The caregiver's threat to quit and never speak to the widow again likely impaired the widow's judgment and persuaded her to sell the caregiver her business. This is further evidenced by the below-market sales price (unfair bargain) and the widow's age and poor health (susceptibility). Therefore, the son is most likely to prevail on this basis.

(Choice A) DuressDuress (胁迫) renders a contract voidablevoidable (可撤销的) if a party's assent was induced by an improper threatimproper threat (不正当威胁) that left the party with no reasonable alternative but to succumb to that threat. Here, even if the caregiver's threat was improper, the widow had a reasonable alternative (eg, hiring a new caregiver).

(Choice B) A person placed under another's guardianshipguardianship (监护) lacks the capacitycapacity (行为能力) to contract, so a contract entered by that person is void (not merely voidable). But here, the widow was placed under the son's guardianship after she agreed to sell her business to the caregiver.

(Choice C) A contract is voidablevoidable (可撤销的) for a misrepresentationmisrepresentation (虚假陈述) that (1) was fraudulent or material, (2) induced assent to the contract, and (3) was justifiably relied on by the assenting party. But since the widow knew other caregivers were available, her reliance on the caregiver's misrepresentation was unjustified.

📌 Educational Objective

Undue influence renders a contract voidable when assent stemmed from unfair or excessive persuasion by someone who dominated or shared a special relationship of trust and confidence with the assenting party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 177 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when undue influence makes a contract voidable).
questions.zh-question:
一位年迈的寡妇有一个成年儿子，住在州外。寡妇健康状况不佳，因此她雇佣了一名住家护工来照料她的日常需求。护工得知寡妇拥有一家成功的面包店，便与寡妇交好，以说服她将面包店卖给自己。当寡妇后来决定将面包店卖给她的儿子时，护工变得很不高兴。她谎称寡妇所在的社区没有其他可靠的护工。然后，护工威胁说，除非寡妇同意将面包店卖给她，否则她将辞职并且再也不和寡妇说话。尽管寡妇知道有其他护工可选，但她依赖这名护工，并且害怕失去她。因此，寡妇签署了一份合同，以低于市场价值一半的价格将面包店卖给了护工。

此后不久，寡妇被置于其儿子的监护之下。当儿子了解到这份合同以及护工的威胁后，他代表寡妇提起诉讼，要求撤销该合同。

儿子最有可能基于什么理由胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 胁迫。
zh-choices.B: 缺乏（缔约）能力。
zh-choices.C: 虚假陈述。
zh-choices.D: 不当影响。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：不当影响（undue influence），也就是一方靠“控制关系 + 不公平施压”把对方逼着签合同，所以合同可撤销。

三秒认题路径：

照护依赖 → 关系失衡 → 不公平施压 → 合同可撤销 → 选 D

核心法律规则

不当影响（undue influence）是指：一方的同意来自对方的不公平或过度劝诱（unfair or excessive persuasion），而且对方还处在支配地位，或者双方有特别的信赖关系。考场意思：不是单纯“说服”，而是已经把对方的独立判断压扁了。

弱势性（susceptibility）、不公平交易（unfair bargain）、缺少独立建议（independent advice），都会把这类题推向不当影响。考场意思：老人、病弱、严重吃亏、又没人帮她独立判断，通常就是高危信号。

所以这题里，关键不是“有没有威胁”本身，而是 caregiver 利用照护依赖和恐惧，把 widow 推到一个根本没法冷静决定的位置。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 177 直接锁定：被支配关系中的不公平施压，会让合同成为可撤销。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“单纯不爽就反悔”?
不是。 要先找有没有不当影响（undue influence）的控制关系。
关卡 1：有没有支配 / 信赖关系？
有。 live-in caregiver 负责日常照护，widow 对她有现实依赖。
关卡 2：有没有不公平施压？
有。 “辞职 + 不再说话”再加上虚假说法，已经不是正常谈判。
关卡 3：结果是否明显吃亏？
有。 售价低于市价一半，直接提示 bargain 很不公平。
卡死点：这不是 duress，因为 widow 仍有别的 caregiver 可选；也不是 lack of capacity，因为监护是在签约后才开始。
结论：合同为何可撤销？
因为。 对方靠关系优势压住判断力，答案就是 D. Undue influence。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她被“威胁”了，所以应该选 duress。

但考试真正问的是：caregiver 有没有借着照护关系，把 widow 的判断力压到失控，而不是看她是不是被逼到“完全没路可走”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里 caregiver 先建立依赖，再用辞职和虚假说法压迫 widow，最后又卖出 less than half its market value，这正是 不当影响（undue influence）。

❌ 法律适用 | 胁迫门槛误判

✕ A: 把 no reasonable alternative 想得太满；这里她还有别的 caregiver 可找。

❌ 事实误判 | 监护时间偷换

✕ B: 把 guardianship 提前到签约前了；题干写得很清楚，监护是在之后才开始。

❌ 概念混淆 | 依赖类型混淆

✕ C: 把 misrepresentation 当成万能钥匙；她明知还有其他照护者，不能说是正当依赖。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓关系控制，再看是否有不公平施压和明显吃亏，最后排掉胁迫、能力和虚假陈述。

考场速记

记住：不当影响（undue influence）看的是“关系优势 + 过度施压 + 判断力被压扁”；胁迫（duress）看的是“非法威胁 + 没有合理替代”。

口诀：Undue influence = trust + pressure + unfair deal。以后看到照护、依赖、低价成交，先想 D。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
A toy company contracted with a manufacturer to produce gel packets used to simulate water in its faux aquarium toy. On May 1, in a writing signed by both parties, the manufacturer agreed to deliver 1 million gel packets for a total price of $1 million to be paid on June 1, the date of delivery. The writing specified that any modification of its terms required the toy company's signed, written consent.
On May 15, the manufacturer called the toy company to explain that it was running low on raw material and would need more time to produce the desired quantity of gel packets. The parties agreed in the telephone conversation to postpone the delivery date to July 1. On July 1, the manufacturer delivered the gel packets to the toy company, which refused to accept or pay for them.
Is the manufacturer likely to prevail in a breach-of-contract suit against the toy company?

choices.A: No, because any modification to the parties' agreement required the toy company's signed, written consent.
choices.B: No, because there was no consideration to support the May 15 agreement.
choices.C: Yes, because the manufacturer reasonably relied on the toy company's having waived the signed-writing requirement.
choices.D: Yes, because the May 15 agreement was enforceable under the statute of frauds.

questions.explanation:
"No oral modification" (NOM) clause
Common law (contracts for services
or real estate)
  • NOM clause enforceable only if modification must be in writing under statute of frauds
UCC (contracts for sale of
goods)
  • All parties are merchants – NOM clause always enforceable
  • ≥ 1 party is nonmerchant – NOM clause in merchant's form must be separately signed by nonmerchant(s) to be enforceable
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

The UCC statute of frauds applies to contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more (eg, 1 million gel packets for $1 million) and renders them unenforceable unless they are in a writing that:

  • provides a reasonable basis to believe a contract was formed
  • states the quantity of goods to be sold and
  • is signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

Modifications to a contract that falls within and satisfies this statute generally need not be in writing because the enforceability of the initial contract passes to any modifications. However, the UCC will enforce a "no oral modification" (NOM) clause that requires modifications to be in writing. A NOM clause can be waived by the parties through words or conduct, and the waiver cannot be retracted if a party has materially changed its position in reasonable reliance on the waiver.

Here, the parties' May 1 contract fell within and satisfied the statute of frauds. As a result, their May 15 oral agreement did not violate this statute (Choice D). Although the contract contained a NOM clause that prohibited modifications without the toy company's written consent, the toy company waived the clause on May 15 by orally agreeing to postpone the delivery date to July 1 (Choice A). And since the manufacturer materially and reasonably relied on the waiver by delivering the gel packets on that date, it will likely prevail.

(Choice B) Consideration is not required to modify a contract for the sale of goods, but any modification must be sought in good faith and comply with reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing.

📌 Educational Objective

The UCC will enforce a "no oral modification" (NOM) clause even if the modification would not otherwise need to be in a writing that satisfies the statute of frauds. NOM clauses can be waived through the parties' words or conduct, and the waiver cannot be retracted if a party has materially changed position in reasonable reliance on the waiver.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-201 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (formal requirements for the statute of frauds).
  • U.C.C. § 2-209 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (modification, rescission, and waiver).
questions.zh-question:
一家玩具公司与一家制造商签订合同，生产用于在其仿真水族馆玩具中模拟水的凝胶包。

5月1日，在一份由双方签署的书面文件中，制造商同意交付100万个凝胶包，总价为100万美元，于6月1日交货日支付。该书面文件规定，对其条款的任何修改均需获得玩具公司签署的书面同意。

5月15日，制造商致电玩具公司，解释其原材料短缺，需要更多时间来生产所需数量的凝胶包。双方在电话交谈中同意将交货日期推迟至7月1日。7月1日，制造商将凝胶包交付给玩具公司，但玩具公司拒绝接收或付款。

在该制造商对玩具公司提起的违约诉讼中，制造商是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为对双方协议的任何修改都需要玩具公司签署的书面同意。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为没有对价来支持5月15日的协议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为制造商合理地信赖了玩具公司已放弃签署书面文件的要求。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为根据《反欺诈法》，5月15日的协议是可强制执行的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC货物买卖合同里的no oral modification（NOM）条款能不能被口头放弃，以及对方能否因合理依赖而把这个放弃“锁死”。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 有NOM条款 → 口头改期 → 对方依赖 → 还能主张履行

核心法律规则

只看这条规则就够了

这是货物买卖合同（sale of goods contract），适用UCC；金额达到或超过500美元时，原合同要满足statute of frauds，但一旦书面合同已经成立，后续修改通常不必再写进新书面里。

no oral modification（NOM）条款考场意思：合同可以自己先写死“改动必须书面同意”，但当事人也可能用口头话或行为把这条要求waive（放弃）掉；一旦另一方已经基于这个放弃做了实质依赖，就不能轻易撤回。

所以这题不是在问“口头改约有没有对价”，而是在问：toy company 先口头同意把交货日延到 July 1，再让 manufacturer 按这个新安排发货，自己就很难再拿原来的书面限制挡人。

核心判例： UCC § 2-209 的思路锁定本题：NOM 条款能生效，但也能被口头或行为放弃；合理依赖一出现，撤回就卡住。

思维导图

先看：这是不是要立刻回到“书面修改必须存在”的题？
YES不是。因为 May 1 的书面已经满足 UCC 的 statute of frauds，所以 May 15 的口头改期不需要重新过 SOF。
NO再看合同里有没有 NOM 条款：有，而且它本来要求改动要书面同意。
关键 toy company 口头同意延到 July 1，本质上是在放弃（waive）书面同意要求。
最后 manufacturer 已按这个放弃去生产并交货，出现合理且实质依赖，撤回失败。
结论：选 C，manufacturer 更可能赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然合同明写“修改必须书面同意”，那口头改期当然没效。

但考试真正问的是：toy company 自己后来有没有把这条书面要求给放弃掉，而且 manufacturer 是否已经按这个放弃去行动了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里同样是看规则有没有被 waiver 和 reliance 重新改写，不是机械盯着最初那句条款。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 口头同意把交货日延到 July 1，已经构成对 NOM 条款的放弃；manufacturer 随后发货并依赖这一安排，所以 toy company 很难反悔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 条款效力误判

✕ A: 只盯着 signed, written consent，没看到条款后来已被口头放弃。

❌ 法律适用 | 对价要求误判

✕ B: 货物买卖的修改不靠新增对价卡关，真正卡的是 waiver 和依赖。

❌ 事实误判 | SOF结论偷换

✕ D: 把 statute of frauds 当成改约门槛，但原合同已合规，争点在后续放弃。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“原合同是否满足 SOF”与“后续 NOM 是否被 waiver”，再看对方有没有合理依赖。

考场速记

记住：UCC 货物合同里，NOM 条款能管住口头修改，但也可能被口头行为放弃；一旦对方已经依赖，就别再想把门关回去。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，记的是中间上诉例外；这题不是上诉题，但同样要先找“例外有没有把默认规则改掉”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In a telephone conversation, a jewelry maker offered to buy 100 ounces of gold from a precious metals company if delivery could be made within 10 days. The jewelry maker did not specify a price, but the market price for 100 ounces of gold at the time of the conversation was approximately $65,000. Without otherwise responding, the company delivered the gold six days later.
In the meantime, the project for which the jewelry maker planned to use the gold was canceled. The jewelry maker therefore refused to accept delivery of the gold or to pay the $65,000 demanded by the company.
Is there an enforceable contract between the jewelry maker and the company?

choices.A: No, because the parties did not agree on a price term.
choices.B: No, because the parties did not put their agreement in writing.
choices.C: Yes, because the absence of a price term does not defeat the formation of a valid contract for the sale of goods where the parties otherwise intended to form a contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the company relied on an implied promise to pay when it delivered the gold.

questions.explanation:
The UCC statute of frauds applies to contracts for the sale of goods of $500 or more (eg, gold valued at $65,000—as seen here) and renders such contracts unenforceable unless they are in a writing that:

  • provides a reasonable basis to believe a contract was formed
  • states the quantity of goods to be sold* and
  • is signed with an identifying mark by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

However, this statute does not apply when (1) the goods are specially manufactured, (2) the party against whom enforcement is sought admits to the contract, or (3) some amount of payment or goods was received and accepted.

Here, there is no indication that the gold was specially manufactured for the jewelry maker or that the jewelry maker admitted to a contract with the company. And though the company delivered the gold to the jewelry maker, the jewelry maker refused to accept delivery. Therefore, the contract is not excepted from the statute of frauds. And since the parties did not put their agreement into writing, it is unenforceable.

*The contract is only enforceable up to the written quantity.

(Choices A & C) A contract for the sale of goods is enforceable even if the price term is missing or incorrectly stated. But even though the absence of a price term does not affect the enforceability of the contract between the jewelry maker and the company, the contract is still unenforceable because the parties failed to put it in writing.

(Choice D) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, the company's reliance on an implied promise to pay would provide an alternative basis for recovery only if such reliance was reasonable and caused the company substantial detriment (eg, turning down substantial business to fulfill the jewelry maker's request—not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts for the sale of goods of $500 or more are not subject to the statute of frauds if (1) the goods are specially manufactured, (2) the party against whom enforcement is sought admits to the contract, or (3) some amount of goods or payment was received and accepted.

📚 References
  • UCC § 2-201 (statute of frauds formal requirements).
questions.zh-question:
在一次电话交谈中，一位珠宝制造商向一家贵金属公司要约购买100盎司黄金，条件是在10天内完成交付。该珠宝制造商没有明确价格，但通话时100盎司黄金的市场价格约为65,000美元。该公司未作其他回应，在六天后交付了黄金。

与此同时，珠宝制造商计划使用这批黄金的项目被取消了。因此，该珠宝制造商拒绝接受黄金的交付，也拒绝支付公司要求的65,000美元。

珠宝制造商与该公司之间是否存在一份可强制执行的合同？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为双方当事人未就价格条款达成一致。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为双方当事人未将其协议以书面形式订立。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在双方当事人有意订立合同的情况下，缺少价格条款并不妨碍一份有效的货物销售合同的成立。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为公司在交付黄金时信赖了一项默示的付款承诺。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Statute of frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：货物买卖（sale of goods）达到 $500以上 时，UCC 书面形式要件（statute of frauds）卡住的是“能不能强制执行”，不是“有没有谈成价格”。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 金额超500 → 看书面 → 查例外 → 仍然无效

核心法律规则

UCC 书面形式要件（statute of frauds）适用于货物买卖（sale of goods）且金额为 $500或以上 的合同；考场意思：先别管价格谈没谈拢，只要落进这个门槛，通常就要看书面。

书面至少要能看出有合同、写明数量，并由被要求执行的一方签名；考场意思：不是长篇合同也行，但要有“这单有多少、谁被绑住”的痕迹。

例外只有几种：特制货物（specially manufactured goods）、承认合同（admission）、或一部分货物/价款已被收受并接受；考场意思：本题里卖家只是送货，买家没收货，所以例外没被触发。

核心判例： UCC § 2-201 — 这条规则直接锁定：没有书面，又没有例外，不可强制执行（unenforceable）。

思维导图

先看：这是 货物买卖（sale of goods） 吗？且金额是否 $500以上？
是进入 UCC statute of frauds。
再看：有没有书面，能写出 数量（quantity） 并带签名？
没有 卡死：默认 unenforceable，不能强制执行。
最后查例外：specially manufactured / admission / received and accepted？
本题只有“送货”这一面向，但买家没接受货物，例外不成立。
结论：选 B：没写书面，所以不能执行。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然没有约定价格，合同是不是根本没成立，所以应选“价格缺失”那个选项。

但考试真正问的是：书面形式要件（statute of frauds）有没有卡死执行，不是合同谈判里少了一个价格条款。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个坑是把“卖方已经送货”误看成例外；真正需要的是收到并接受（received and accepted），而买家这里明确拒收。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 100 盎司黄金约 $65,000，已落入 UCC 书面形式要件（statute of frauds），又没有书面，所以不能执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 price term 当成门槛，错把形成问题和执行问题混在一起。

❌ 法律适用 | 形成规则误套

✕ C: 只盯着“能不能成立”，却漏掉了 put it in writing 这一层。

❌ 事实误判 | 接受条件偷换

✕ D: 把 implied promise 说成代替书面，但题干没给出足够依赖损害事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定是否进 UCC 书面形式要件（statute of frauds），再逐个排例外，不要被价格条款带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“货物超五百，先问书面；没书面，先看例外；没例外，就不能强制执行。”

看到 sale of goods + $500，脑中先亮 UCC § 2-201，再查“书面、签名、数量、例外”四步。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In a written and signed contract, a buyer agreed to purchase Lot 1 in a subdivision from a developer. Unbeknownst to either party, there was an error in the subdivision's recorded plat, and two separate lots had each been designated as "Lot 1." The buyer intended to purchase the Lot 1 located in the southern half of the subdivision, while the developer intended to sell the Lot 1 located in the northern half of the subdivision. On the day of the closing, the developer presented the buyer with a deed for the northern Lot 1.
Which of the following statements concerning this exchange is accurate?

choices.A: The buyer can enforce the contract for the sale of the northern Lot 1 if he waives the misunderstanding and adopts the developer's understanding of "Lot 1."
choices.B: The buyer can enforce the contract for the sale of the southern Lot 1, because the risk of a plat error can be allocated to the developer that created the plat.
choices.C: The developer can enforce the contract for the sale of the northern Lot 1, because it did not know or have reason to know of the buyer's interpretation of "Lot 1" when the contract was made.
choices.D: The parties must seek reformation of the contract, and the court will decide which of the plats is the true "Lot 1."

questions.explanation:
Misunderstanding of material term
General rule Waiver
Neither / both parties know of misunderstanding No contract formed Either party can enforce other party's understanding
One party knows of misunderstanding Contract formed based on unknowing party's understanding Unknowing party can enforce knowing party's understanding

A misunderstanding arises when there is no meeting of the minds because the parties to a contract assign different meanings to the same term. Where the misunderstanding involves a material term and neither party (or both parties) knew or had reason to know of the misunderstanding, ordinarily there is no contract. However, either party can waive the misunderstanding and choose to enforce the contract in accordance with the other party's understanding.

Here, the buyer and the developer assigned different meanings to the term "Lot 1." Neither party was aware of the misunderstanding, and there is no indication that either of them had reason to know of the misunderstanding. Although this would ordinarily result in no contract, the buyer can waive his own misunderstanding to enforce the contract for the sale of the northern Lot 1—the developer's understanding of "Lot 1."

(Choice B) A court can allocate the risk of a mistake—ie, an erroneous belief of fact held by one or both parties—to a party upon a finding that it is reasonable in the circumstances to do so (eg, based on that party's culpability). But a court cannot allocate the risk of a misunderstanding—ie, the attachment of different meanings to the same term.

(Choice C) The developer cannot enforce the sale of the northern Lot 1 simply because he was unaware of the buyer's misinterpretation. And though the developer could waive the misunderstanding, this would allow the developer to enforce the contract based on the buyer's understanding (the southern Lot 1)—not the developer's understanding (the northern Lot 1).

(Choice D) When a writing fails to reflect the true meaning of the parties, either party may ask the court to reform the contract to accurately express the parties' agreement. But such reformation is generally a remedy for a mistake, not a misunderstanding.

📌 Educational Objective

A misunderstanding involving a material term ordinarily results in no contract if neither (or both) parties knew or had reason to know of the misunderstanding. However, one party can waive the misunderstanding and enforce the contract in accordance with the other party's understanding.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 20 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of misunderstanding).
questions.zh-question:
在一份书面且经签署的合同中，一位买方同意从一位开发商处购买一个分区中的“地块1”。双方当事人均不知情的是，该分区的登记图则中存在一个错误，并且有两个独立的地块均被指定为“地块1”。买方意图购买位于该分区南半部的“地块1”，而开发商意图出售位于该分区北半部的“地块1”。在交割日当天，开发商向买方出示了北部“地块1”的地契。

关于此次交易，以下哪项陈述是准确的？

zh-choices.A: 如果买方放弃对误解的主张，并采纳开发商对“地块1”的理解，则买方可以强制执行出售北部“地块1”的合同。
zh-choices.B: 买方可以强制执行出售南部“地块1”的合同，因为法院可以合理地将图则错误的风险分配给开发商。
zh-choices.C: 开发商可以强制执行出售北部“地块1”的合同，因为在订立合同时，其没有理由知道买方对“地块1”的解释。
zh-choices.D: 任何一方当事人都不能强制执行该合同，因为他们对一个重要条款的不同解释导致合同可被撤销。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Mistake & misunderstanding

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：同一个合同用语出现 material misunderstanding（重大误解） 时，哪一方可以“放弃自己的理解”，改按对方的理解去执行合同。

三秒认题路径：

同词异义 → 双方不知 → 原则无合同 → 但可放弃 → 按对方理解

核心法律规则

如果双方对同一个 material term（重要条款） 赋予了不同意思，这叫 misunderstanding（误解），考场意思：不是谁记错事实，而是“同一个词，脑子里装的不是一回事”。

若双方都不知道，也没有理由知道这个误解，通常no contract（无合同）；但任一方都可以 waive（放弃） 误解，转而按对方理解来强制执行。

这题里，买方和开发商都把 Lot 1 理解成不同地块，而且双方都不知情，所以默认结果是无合同；但买方可以放弃自己的理解，改按开发商理解去要求北边那块地。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 20 这一规则直接锁定本题：重大误解下，能否执行看“是否有人放弃自己的理解”。

思维导图

同一词语出现不同理解：Lot 1 是不是双方说的不是同一块地？
第一问：双方都不知道，也都没有理由知道？
是 → 默认：no contract；但不是死局。
第二问：有没有一方愿意 waive 自己的误解？
有 → 该方可以按对方理解去执行合同。
本题落点：买方放弃自己的“南边 Lot 1”，改按开发商的“北边 Lot 1”主张。
结论 → 选 A。
易错点：不要把 mistake（错误） 和 misunderstanding（误解） 混成一题。
前者可谈风险分配；后者先看“词义不一致”，再看谁能放弃。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：双方都没看懂，当然应该去找法院“改合同”或“分配风险”。

但考试真正问的是：这不是单纯的事实错误，而是 misunderstanding；先看谁能放弃自己的理解，再决定按哪一边的意思执行。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 Lot 1 同词异义 属于双方都不知的误解；买方可以放弃自己的理解，按开发商理解要求北边那块地。

❌ 概念混淆 | 风险分配误判

✕ B: 把 plat error 当成可分配风险的错误，忽略了本题考的是误解不是错误。

❌ 法律适用 | 单方理解误判

✕ C: 只盯着开发商不知道买方想法，却忘了无知的一方不能单方面抢用自己的理解。

❌ 事实误判 | 误把合同改写

✕ D: 把 reformation 当成误解救济，但这题不是写错字，而是双方意思本来就不一致。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是 mistake 还是 misunderstanding，再看是否有人愿意放弃自己的解释。

考场速记

记住一句：同词异义先看误解，没人知情默认无合同；有人愿意让步，就按对方意思执行。

本题口诀：waive the misunderstanding, enforce the other side。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A 17-year-old boy started a business mowing lawns for his neighbors. As the boy's business grew, he received requests for lawn services from homeowners in neighborhoods located several miles away. The boy lived with his parents and had use of the family's old pickup truck after 4:00 p.m. each day to carry his lawn maintenance equipment to the other neighborhoods. However, the boy believed that it was necessary to own a truck that could be used for his business at any hour. He therefore entered a contract with a used-car dealership to purchase a truck.
Which of the following statements best describes the contract between the boy and the used-car dealership?

choices.A: The contract for necessaries is enforceable.
choices.B: The contract is voidable only by the boy.
choices.C: The contract is voidable by either party.
choices.D: The contract is void and unenforceable.

questions.explanation:
An unmarried, unemancipated minor (ie, person under the age of 18) lacks capacity to contract, so any contract entered by the minor is voidable by the minor. However, the contract is not voidable by the other contracting party. This means that the minor has the sole power to either:

  • void the contract before or soon after turning 18 by (1) disaffirming the contract through words or actions and (2) returning any still-existing benefit received under the contract or
  • ratify the contract after turning 18 by (1) failing to timely void the contract or (2) otherwise agreeing to be bound by it.

However, if the minor seeks to void a contract for necessaries, then the minor can still incur liability for the reasonable value of the necessaries under a quasi-contract theory. "Necessaries" is a flexible term that generally includes food, clothing, shelter, and anything else that (1) is actually required for the minor's support or well-being and (2) has not been provided by the minor's parent or guardian.

Here, the 17-year-old boy contracted with the dealership to purchase a truck because he believed that it was necessary to own a truck that could be used for his business. But the boy did not actually require a new truck because he had use of the family's pickup truck to carry his lawn maintenance equipment to other neighborhoods. Therefore, the necessaries exception does not apply here, and the contract is voidable only by the boy (Choices A, C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

Minors lack capacity to contract, so a contract entered by a minor is voidable by the minor. However, a minor who chooses to disaffirm a contract for necessaries (eg, food, clothing, shelter) must pay for their reasonable value.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 14 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (incapacity based on infancy).
  • 42 Am. Jur. 2d Infants §§ 56–63 (2020) (infant liability for necessaries).
  • 42 Am. Jur. 2d Infants §§ 64–69 (2020) (examples of necessaries).
questions.zh-question:
一个17岁的男孩开始为他的邻居修剪草坪作为生意。随着男孩生意的增长，他收到了几英里外社区的房主提出的草坪服务请求。这个男孩和他的父母住在一起，每天下午4点以后可以使用家里的旧皮卡车，将他的草坪维护设备运到其他社区。然而，男孩认为有必要拥有一辆可以在任何时间用于其生意的卡车。因此，他与一家二手车经销商签订了购买卡车的合同。

以下哪项陈述最准确地描述了男孩与二手车经销商之间的合同？

zh-choices.A: 该必需品合同是可强制执行的。
zh-choices.B: 该合同仅可由男孩单方面撤销。
zh-choices.C: 该合同可由任何一方撤销。
zh-choices.D: 该合同无效且不可强制执行。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：未成年人签的买卖合同通常只能由未成年人单方撤销，只有“必需品（necessaries）”例外才会让他对合理价额负责。

三秒认题路径：

17岁未成年 → 先看能力 → 默认可撤销 → 再查必需品 → 本题选 B

核心法律规则

未婚、未成年且未被解放的未成年人（未成年人（minor））通常缺乏缔约能力，所以他签的合同一般只是可撤销（voidable），而且只有他自己能撤销，另一方不能替他撤销。考试上你要先记住：这里不是“合同天然无效”，而是“先能成立，但未成年人有反悔权”。

如果合同标的是必需品（necessaries），未成年人即使撤销，也可能要按合理价额（reasonable value）承担责任；但前提是这东西真的用于其生活或健康需要，而且父母或监护人没有提供。这里的 necessaries 不是“他觉得业务上方便”就算，而是“对这个孩子现在真的必须”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 14 锁定规则：未成年人默认可撤销，必需品例外只让他承担合理价额，不把合同变成双方都能撤销。

思维导图

17岁未成年签了买车合同，先问：这份合同是谁能撤销？
第一关：未成年人是否有缔约能力？
没有 → 默认合同 voidable，而且只可由未成年人撤销
第二关：是不是 necessaries？
不是：他家里已有旧皮卡，车只是“更方便做生意”
结论：不触发必需品例外 → 不是双方都能撤销，也不是自动无效
正确答案：voidable only by the boy

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他买的是做生意要用的车，看起来很“必要”，所以合同应算 necessaries。

但考试真正问的是：这辆车是不是这个未成年人“真实缺少、而且父母没提供”的必需品；题干已经告诉你他家里有旧皮卡可用，所以只是商业上更方便，不是法律上的必需品。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上有没有更好用的工具」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是 17岁且只是想让生意更方便，不是实际缺少生活所需，所以合同只能由男孩自己撤销。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“业务需要”直接等同 necessaries 了。

❌ 法律适用 | 双方可撤销误判

✕ C: 以为卖车商也能反悔撤销，但未成年人合同的反悔权不对称。

❌ 事实误判 | 自动无效偷换

✕ D: 把未成年人的合同误当成 void，其实只是可撤销。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓缔约能力，再扫“必需品”例外；只要题干有替代供给，就别把“方便”当成“必要”。

考场速记

记住一句：未成年人合同默认可撤销，只有未成年人能撤销；必需品例外只改赔偿，不改这道题的基本结论。 如果题目在问中间上诉类例外，才去背 In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely；但本题不是上诉题，直接盯“未成年 + 必需品”就够了。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A real estate developer solicited bids from general contractors to build residences on 50 lots owned by the developer. A general contractor, in turn, solicited bids from subcontractors for the various aspects of the construction process. A company submitted a bid of $1 million for performing the electrical work. This bid was based on a careless omission of the cost of an electrical component called for in the specifications prepared by the developer. The other bids received by the general contractor for the electrical work ranged from $1.25 million to $1.3 million, which were in line with the general contractor's own estimate for the electrical work. The general contractor used the company's bid of $1 million for performing the electrical work in submitting its bid to the developer.
After the general contractor's bid was accepted by the developer and the general contractor, in turn, accepted the company's bid, but before any work on the residences began, the company discovered its error. Although the company will make no profit from the job instead of the $100,000 profit it would have made had it correctly read the specifications, enforcement of its contract with the general contractor would not be unconscionable.
Is it likely that the company can avoid the contract?

choices.A: No, because the company's bid was based on its own carelessness in computing its bid.
choices.B: No, because the enforcement of the contract would not be unconscionable.
choices.C: Yes, because the general contractor had reason to know of the mistake.
choices.D: Yes, because there was a misunderstanding that prevented the formation of the contract.

questions.explanation:
A valid contract is generally formed when a mutual agreement is supported by adequate consideration, such as when the general contractor accepted the company's bid of $1 million for performing the electrical work. Although the company omitted the cost of an item when computing its bid, its unilateral mistake is not grounds to avoid the contract unless:

  • the mistake would make enforcement of the contract against the nonmistaken party unconscionable (eg, due to a substantial difference between contract price and actual value) or
  • the nonmistaken party caused, or knew or had reason to know of, the mistake.

Here, the facts stipulate that enforcement of the contract would not be unconscionable ((Choice B)). But the other bids received by the general contractor ranged from $1.25 million to $1.3 million—a 25% to 30% discrepancy from the company's bid. Since the other bids were in line with the general contractor's own estimate for the electrical work, the general contractor had reason to know that the company's $1 million bid was based on a mistake. As a result, the company can likely avoid the contract.

(Choice A) The mistaken party's negligence with regard to its mistake (eg, the company's careless computing of its bid) does not prevent that party from avoiding the contract.

(Choice D) A misunderstanding occurs when the parties attach different meanings to the same material term (eg, price). Here, the erroneous $1 million bid did not create a misunderstanding that would prevent contract formation since "$1 million" has just one meaning.

📌 Educational Objective

Unilateral mistake is not grounds to avoid a contract unless (1) the mistake would make enforcement of the contract unconscionable or (2) the nonmistaken party caused, or knew or had reason to know of, the mistake.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 153 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when unilateral mistake makes a contract voidable).
questions.zh-question:
一位房地产开发商为其拥有的50块地块上的住宅建设向总承包商招标。总承包商随即就施工过程中的各个方面向分包商招标。一家公司提交了一份100万美元的电气工程投标。该投标是基于其在计算中疏忽遗漏了开发商制定的规格说明书中要求的一项电气组件的成本。总承包商收到的其他电气工程投标报价在125万美元到130万美元之间，这与总承包商自己对电气工程的估价相符。总承包商在向开发商提交其总投标时，采用了这家公司100万美元的电气工程报价。

在开发商接受了总承包商的投标，并且总承包商也接受了该公司的投标之后，但在住宅工程开始前，该公司发现了自己的错误。尽管该公司将无法从此项工作中获利，而不是如果其正确阅读规格说明书本可以获得的10万美元利润，但强制执行其与总承包商的合同并不会构成不合情理。

该公司是否有可能撤销该合同？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为公司的投标是基于其自身在计算投标时的疏忽。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为强制执行该合同不会构成不合情理。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为总承包商有理由知道这个错误的存在。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为存在误解，导致合同未能成立。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to enforceability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：单方错误（unilateral mistake）什么时候能让投标方撤掉合同，重点看对方是否知道或应知这个错误。

三秒认题路径：

投标报错 → 单方错误 → 对方应知 → 合同可撤销 → 选 Yes

核心法律规则

单方错误（unilateral mistake）一般不能随便毁约；考场上先看两条门：一是继续履行会不会对没犯错的一方unconscionable，也就是硬要照做会不会太离谱；二是没犯错的一方有没有造成、知道，或本该知道这个错误。

如果这两条里至少一条成立，合同就可能变成可撤销（voidable）。本题里法院已说履行不算unconscionable，所以真正的突破口只剩“对方是否应知”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 153 — 单方错误可撤销的关键就是“对方造成/知道/应知”或“履行明显不公”。

思维导图

先问：这是单方错误（unilateral mistake）吗？
是 投标人自己把电气组件成本漏掉了，错在自己这边。
再问：履行会不会对对方unconscionable？
否 题目已经直接说：不会。这条门被卡死，不能靠“太不公平”撤约。
最后问：没犯错的一方有没有知道或应知（knew or had reason to know）？
是 总包看到其他分包报价都在 $1.25M 到 $1.3M，和自己估价一致，只有这家报 $1M，这正是“应知有错”的信号。
结论：合同可撤销，答案选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方自己算错了，而且还是careless，所以不能反悔。

但考试真正问的是：对方有没有理由看出来这是一张报错的标，而不是单看“谁更粗心”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

总包拿到的其他电气报价都在 $1.25M 到 $1.3M，和这家 $1M 明显不一致，所以它应知（had reason to know）这里报错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 过失否认错

✕ A: 只盯着carelessness，把“自己算错”误当成不能撤约的绝对障碍。

❌ 法律适用 | 不公平门槛误判

✕ B: 把“不是unconscionable”当成终点，漏掉了“对方应知”这条独立通道。

❌ 事实误判 | 误解混同错拿

✕ D: 把单纯报错说成misunderstanding，但这里不是双方对同一词语有不同理解。

这题建议用什么方法？

先排“是否不公平”，再抓“对方是否应知”，不要被“谁更粗心”带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：单方错误（unilateral mistake）不是自动撤约，要么太不公平，要么对方知道/应知才有戏；看到总包报价明显低得离谱，就要立刻想到“应知有错”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
A father and his adult daughter encountered an old family friend on the street. The daughter said to the family friend, "How about lending me $1,000 to buy a used car? I'll pay you back with interest one year from today." The father added, "And if she doesn't pay it back as promised, I will." The family friend thereupon wrote out and handed to the daughter his personal check, payable to her, for $1,000, and she subsequently used the funds to buy a used car. When the debt came due, both the daughter and the father refused to repay any part of it.
In an action by the family friend against the father to recover $1,000 plus interest, which of the following statements would summarize the father's best defense?

choices.A: He received no consideration for his conditional promise to the family friend.
choices.B: His conditional promise to the family friend was not made for the primary purpose of benefiting himself (the father).
choices.C: His conditional promise to the family friend was not to be performed in less than a year from the time it was made.
choices.D: The loan by the family friend was made without any agreement concerning the applicable interest rate.

questions.explanation:
Contracts subject to the statute of frauds are enforceable only if they are (1) in a writing that provides a reasonable basis to believe a contract was formed and (2) signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. Here, the check from the family friend may have satisfied the writing requirement. But since it was not signed by the father, the contract is unenforceable if it is subject to the statute of frauds.

A suretyship is a promise to assume responsibility for a duty incurred by another (eg, the father's promise to pay the loan if the daughter does not). Under the main-purpose rule, suretyships are subject to the statute of frauds unless they are made for the promisor's own economic advantage. Therefore, the father's best defense is that his suretyship was primarily made to benefit his daughter, so it is subject to and unenforceable under the statute of frauds.

(Choice A) The suretyship is supported by consideration because each promise was induced by the promises of the other parties. The family friend loaned the daughter $1,000 based on both promises to pay him back (and vice versa).

(Choice C) A one-year contract is not subject to the statute of frauds if it is possible to perform within one year (even if the parties agree on a later completion date). Here, it was possible for the daughter or father to pay the loan within a year, so this would not trigger the statute of frauds.

(Choice D) An agreement concerning an applicable interest rate was not needed to form an enforceable contract.

📌 Educational Objective

A suretyship is a promise to assume responsibility for a duty incurred by another. Unless a suretyship is made for the promisor's own economic advantage, it is subject to the statute of frauds—ie, it must be in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 112 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (requirement of suretyship).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 116 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (main-purpose rule).
questions.zh-question:
一位父亲和他的成年女儿在街上遇到了一位老世交。女儿对这位世交说：“可以借我1000美元买一辆二手车吗？我将在一年后的今天连本带息还给你。”父亲补充道：“如果她没有如约偿还，我来还。”于是，这位世交开了一张抬头为女儿、金额为1000美元的个人支票给了她，她随后用这笔钱买了一辆二手车。当债务到期时，女儿和父亲都拒绝偿还任何款项。

在世交对父亲提起的、要求其偿还1000美元及利息的诉讼中，以下哪项陈述是父亲的最佳抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 他对世交的附条件承诺没有获得对价。
zh-choices.B: 他对世交的附条件承诺，其主要目的并非为他自己（父亲）谋利。
zh-choices.C: 他对世交的附条件承诺，自作出承诺起无法在一年内履行完毕。
zh-choices.D: 世交提供的这笔贷款没有就适用的利率达成任何协议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：父亲替女儿还钱的保证债务承诺（suretyship）是否落入防止诈欺法（statute of frauds），以及主要目的规则（main-purpose rule）能不能把它救出去。

三秒认题路径：

替别人还债 → 保证债务 → 先看SOF → 再看例外 → 主要目的不成立

核心法律规则

保证债务承诺（suretyship）就是“如果对方不还，我来还”的承诺，考场意思：这类承诺通常要受防止诈欺法（statute of frauds）管。受 SOF 管的承诺，必须有书面证据，而且要由被起诉的一方签字；这题里，父亲没签字，所以默认不能直接强制执行。

主要目的规则（main-purpose rule）是例外：如果保证承诺主要是为了让承诺人自己得到经济利益，才可能不受 SOF 限制。考场意思：本题父亲是为了帮女儿，不是为了他自己赚钱或保护自己的生意，所以例外不成立。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 112 / § 116 - 这组规则直接锁定：保证债务一般进 SOF，只有主要目的在于承诺人自身经济利益时才可能脱离书面要求。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“我来替别人还”的保证债务（suretyship）？
是 这题里父亲说“她不还，我来还”，正好踩中保证债务。
下一问 有无让防止诈欺法（statute of frauds）失效的例外？
例外检查 主要目的规则没过：父亲是帮女儿，不是为自己经济利益。
书面要求 既然进 SOF，就要书面 + 被起诉方签字；这里只有家族朋友写了支票，不是父亲签的。
结论 父亲最佳抗辩：B，这承诺不是为了他的主要经济利益，所以仍受 SOF 约束。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然父亲也口头答应了，或者这笔钱只是家里借款，那就应该能直接追他还钱。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是一个要先过防止诈欺法（statute of frauds）的保证债务承诺（suretyship），以及主要目的规则（main-purpose rule）有没有把它放出去。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「父亲到底有没有道德上该还」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里父亲说的是“她不还，我来还”，这是典型保证债务承诺；但他的目的只是帮女儿，不是自己的经济利益，所以 SOF 例外不成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 以为没对价

✕ A: 把父亲的抗辩错看成 consideration 问题了。

❌ 法律适用 | 一年规则套错

✕ C: 把 one year 规则搬来，但这题真正争点不是履行期限。

❌ 事实误判 | 利率细节偷换

✕ D: 盯着 interest rate，但利率根本不是这题的成败点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出是不是保证债务，再直接查 SOF 例外里有没有“自己获利”的主要目的。

考场速记

记忆口诀：保证债务（suretyship）先进 SOF，想出去就看主要目的规则（main-purpose rule）是不是在帮自己赚钱。

一句话：替别人还债，默认要书面；只有“我自己也得利”才可能不受限制。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
On June 1, an appliance manufacturer telephoned a supplier to determine whether the supplier could provide 300 washing machine motors of a particular model by October 1. The supplier offered to do so at a price of $300 per motor (a total price of $90,000). The manufacturer's representative said, "Deal." The next day the manufacturer's representative sent the supplier an unsigned note on company letterhead that stated, "I am happy that you are going to supply us with the motors. I will call you soon to talk about another order." The manufacturer then sent catalogs to its regular customers advertising washing machines that included the specified motors.
The manufacturer did not hear from the supplier until July 1, when the supplier called to say that it would be unable to supply the motors because it was no longer carrying that model. At that time, the manufacturer had received no orders for the machines with the specified motors.
The manufacturer sued the supplier for breach of contract, and the supplier raised the statute of frauds as a defense.
Is the supplier's statute of frauds defense likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because the manufacturer distributed the catalogs in reliance on the contract, making the contract enforceable under the statute of frauds.
choices.B: No, because the supplier failed to object to the contents of the note sent by the manufacturer.
choices.C: Yes, because the manufacturer's note failed to contain a signature.
choices.D: Yes, because there is no writing that contains the quantity term of the contract.

questions.explanation:
Statute of frauds requirements
Writing Physical or electronic document(s) containing reasonable basis to believe contract was formed (eg, receipt, check, emails) AND
  • at common law – identifies parties, subject matter, consideration, time & nature of performance
  • under UCC – lists quantity of goods (contract enforceable only up to written quantity)
Signature General rule – handwritten signature from, or other mark identifying, party to be charged (eg, letterhead, electronic signature, initials)
  • Merchant exception – between merchants, written confirmation that satisfies statute of frauds as to sender will bind both parties if no written objection within 10 days
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Under the UCC statute of frauds, contracts for the sale of goods of $500 or more (as seen here) must be in a writing that states the quantity of goods to be sold and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. If the contract is between merchants, then a written confirmation will bind both parties if:

  • the confirmation is sent within a reasonable time
  • the confirmation satisfies the statute of frauds as to the sender and
  • the recipient does not object in writing within 10 days.

Here, the manufacturer's representative sent the supplier an unsigned note on company letterhead to confirm their agreement for the supply of motors. But this confirmation does not satisfy the statute of frauds because it failed to state the quantity of the motors to be sold. Therefore, the supplier's statute-of-frauds defense will succeed.

Had the confirmation listed the quantity of motors being sold, it would have been binding as to both parties and defeated the supplier's statute-of-frauds defense. That is because (1) the manufacturer's letterhead was an identifying mark that satisfied the signature requirement under the statute of frauds and (2) the supplier never objected to the written confirmation (Choices B & C).

(Choice A) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, a party's reliance may serve as an alternative basis for recovery when no valid contract was formed—but it does not make a contract enforceable under the statute of frauds. Additionally, this doctrine only applies if reliance was reasonable and caused substantial detriment (eg, had the manufacturer received orders).

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a written confirmation between merchants satisfies the statute of frauds as to both parties if it (1) is sent within a reasonable time, (2) satisfies the statute of frauds—ie, signed writing with quantity stated—as to the sender, and (3) is not objected to in writing within 10 days.

📚 References
  • UCC § 2-201 (statute of frauds requirements).

制造商起诉供应商违约（breach of contract），供应商则以欺诈法（statute of frauds）作为抗辩。

供应商的欺诈法（statute of frauds）抗辩是否可能成功？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为制造商基于对合同的信赖而分发了产品目录，这使得合同根据“防止欺诈法”可以强制执行。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为供应商未对制造商发送的便条内容提出异议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为制造商的便条没有签名。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为没有任何书面文件包含合同的数量条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC 货物买卖的防欺诈法（statute of frauds）要不要有写明数量的书面确认，才能让商人之间的合同被执行。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 金额超 500 → 看书面 → 看数量 → 看签名

核心法律规则

先抓住规则骨架

UCC 防欺诈法（statute of frauds）管的是货物买卖合同（sale of goods contract），只要价格在 500 美元以上，就必须有书面记录。考场意思：先别看谁赖账，先看有没有能拿来执行的纸面证据。

这个书面必须能看出双方曾经达成交易，而且要写明数量（quantity）；考场意思：数量没写，就算其他内容都像合同，也不够。签名（signature）可以很宽松，信头、缩写、电子标记都可能够用，但这里卡住的是数量，不是签名。

如果是商人之间（between merchants）的书面确认，收到后 10 天内不书面反对，确认书可能同时约束双方；但前提仍是这份确认书本身先满足防欺诈法。考场意思：先过“写没写对”，再谈“对方有没有及时反对”。

核心判例： UCC § 2-201 - 商人之间的确认书能生效，但必须有数量条款；没有数量，就救不了。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 UCC 货物买卖（sale of goods），且价额 ≥ 500？
YES进防欺诈法审查：要书面、要数量、要签名。
书面有无数量？
没有数量 → 直接卡死 → 不能靠这份 note 执行
签名够不够？公司信头可能够，但本题不是死在这里。
商人确认书？没及时书面反对才有用；但前提仍是数量写出来。
结论：数量缺失 → supplier 的 statute of frauds defense 成功 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方发了公司抬头的确认信，而且双方像是已经“谈成”了，应该可以强制执行。

但考试真正问的是：这份书面有没有把数量（quantity）写出来。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「商业上看起来像不像已经成交」。

所以这里不是在比谁更依赖这笔交易，而是在看这张纸能不能先过 statute of frauds 这一关。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 unsigned note 虽然像书面确认，但没有写明 300 个电机的数量，UCC 防欺诈法这一步就过不去。

❌ 概念混淆 | 依赖救济误判

✕ A: 把 promissory estoppel 当成能补齐书面要件了。

❌ 法律适用 | 反对期限误判

✕ B: 只盯着没反对，忽略这封确认信先得写对数量。

❌ 事实误判 | 签名条件偷换

✕ C: 这题不是卡在 signature，而是卡在数量没写。

这题建议用什么方法？

先查货物买卖金额，再盯书面有没有数量，最后才看商人确认书例外。

考场速记

记忆口诀：货物超五百，书面要写数；签名可宽，数量不能无。 商人确认书能救场，但只有先把 quantity 写出来才谈得上 10 天反对规则。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On April 1 of Year 1, a teacher orally agreed with a school principal to teach for nine months beginning on September 1 of Year 1. The agreement required that the teacher be paid $1,000 per month in advance on the first of each month. The teacher taught for eight months, for which he was paid in accordance with the agreement. On May 1 of Year 2, the principal paid the teacher $1,000, but he refused to teach. The principal sued the teacher to recover the $1,000 she had paid him on May 1. In his defense, the teacher pleads the statute of frauds.
Is the teacher's defense likely to be successful?

choices.A: No, because the agreement provided for the teacher to teach for only nine months.
choices.B: No, because the principal had fully performed her obligation under the agreement.
choices.C: Yes, because the agreement could not be completed within one year of its formation.
choices.D: Yes, because the value of his services was more than $500.

questions.explanation:
One-year provision of statute of frauds
Applicability
  • Contracts whose terms make it impossible for any party to fully perform within one year
    • Excludes contracts of uncertain duration (eg, lifetime contracts)
Effect of performance
  • Part performance – does not remove contract from statute, but restitution available for reasonable value of performance rendered
  • Full performance – removes contract from statute, whether or not performance is completed within a year
Effect of option to terminate within a year*
  • Majority rule – does not remove contract from statute, because termination is not performance
  • Minority rule – removes contract from statute, because duration of contract is uncertain
*Jurisdictions agree that where only the plaintiff has the option to terminate, the statute of frauds applies.

Contracts that cannot be performed within one year from the time they are entered due to the constraints of the terms of the agreement are subject to the statute of frauds and therefore must be in writing to be enforceable. However, a party's full performance of its obligations under an oral agreement removes the statute of frauds as a defense.

Here, the teacher and the principal entered into an agreement on April 1 of Year 1. Because the agreement required the teacher to teach through May of Year 2, the agreement could not be performed within one year after it was entered and therefore was subject to the statute of frauds (Choice A). However, the principal made her final payment to the teacher on May 1 of Year 2, thereby fully performing her obligation under the agreement and removing the statute of frauds as a defense (Choice C). Therefore, the teacher's defense will likely not succeed.

(Choice D) A contract for the sale of goods of $500 or more is subject to the statute of frauds. But there is no similar dollar threshold for a contract for services (e.g., teaching).

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts that cannot be performed within one year from the time they are entered are subject to the statute of frauds and thus must be in writing to be enforceable. However, a party's full performance of its obligations under an oral agreement removes the statute of frauds as a defense.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 130 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (providing that when one party to a contract has fully performed its contractual obligations, the one-year provision of the statute of frauds does not prevent enforcement of the promises of other parties).
questions.zh-question:
在Year 1的4月1日，一位老师与一位学校校长口头约定，从Year 1的9月1日开始任教九个月。该协议要求老师每月1日预支1,000美元工资。老师任教了八个月，并按协议获得了报酬。在Year 2的5月1日，校长支付了老师1,000美元，但老师拒绝继续任教。校长起诉老师，要求追回她在5月1日支付给他的1,000美元。老师在抗辩中援引了Statute of Frauds（反欺诈法）。
老师的抗辩是否可能成功？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为协议规定老师只任教九个月。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为校长已完全履行了她在协议项下的义务。
zh-choices.C: 是的，因为该协议无法在协议订立后一年内完成。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为他服务的价值超过500美元。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to enforceability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：口头服务合同虽然可能踩到 一年内不能完成规则（one-year provision），但只要一方已经全部履行（full performance），对方就不能再拿 statute of frauds 当盾牌。

三秒认题路径：

口头合同 → 超过一年 → 看履行 → 一方已全做完 → 不能抗辩

核心法律规则

一年内不能完成规则（one-year provision）只管那些按合同条款看，cannot be performed within one year 的协议，所以要写进书面才可执行。

全部履行（full performance）的考场意思：如果一方已经把自己该做的都做完了，statute of frauds 就不能再帮另一方赖账。

这里老师已经把九个月的教学都做完了，校长一方也已经按月付款到最后一期，所以本题不是“能不能写成书面”的抽象题，而是“对方还能不能继续拿 SOF 拒付”的题。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 130 — 一方完全履行后，one-year provision 不再阻止另一方请求履行。

思维导图

口头服务合同，先问：是不是按条款看“签约后一年内不可能完成”？
是→ 先落入 statute of frauds，通常需要书面。
再问：有没有一方已经 full performance？
卡死点：如果一方已全部履行，SOF 抗辩被拿掉。
本题：教师已教满约定学期，校长也已完成最后付款 → 不能再用 SOF 反悔。
结论：教师抗辩失败，选 No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：合同从 4 月 1 日签起，到次年 5 月才结束，could not be completed within one year，所以一定能用 SOF 胜诉。

但考试真正问的是：一方已经全部履行后，另一方还能不能继续拿 SOF 当挡箭牌。答案是否，因为这里争的不是“合同最初有没有掉进 SOF”，而是“后续履行已经把这个防御拿掉了”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「事实看起来是不是拖过了一年」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 principal paid the teacher 且教师已完成约定教学，说明校长一方已履行完毕，所以不能再靠 statute of frauds 拒绝返还。

❌ 概念混淆 | 期限当成结论

✕ A: 只盯着 nine months，忽略了关键是“一方已全履行”。

❌ 法律适用 | 一年规则误套

✕ C: 把 one year 当成铁定胜点，却没看后面的履行例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 金额门槛偷换

✕ D: 看到 $500 就想到货物买卖，其实这里是服务合同。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓合同类型，再问一方是否已全部履行；只要答案是“是”，SOF 抗辩就会被拆掉。

考场速记

记住一句：先看一年规则，再看有没有 full performance。口头合同如果已经由一方全部做完，statute of frauds 往往不能再救想赖账的人。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A motorcycle collector and his friend had known each other for years. The collector sent a letter to the friend that said, "I am willing to sell you my oldest motorcycle for $4,000." The friend sent the collector an email saying, "I accept your offer." The collector owned three motorcycles: a 1985 model, a 1987 model, and a 1992 model. The friend did not know about the 1985 model, which was the one the collector intended to sell. The collector was unaware that the friend intended to buy the 1987 model. When the collector tendered the 1985 model, the friend refused to accept it.
Is the friend likely to prevail in a breach of contract suit against the collector?

choices.A: No, because by not inquiring further about the meaning of the phrase "oldest motorcycle," the friend assumed the risk of being mistaken.
choices.B: No, because neither the friend nor the collector had reason to know of the other's interpretation of the words "oldest motorcycle."
choices.C: Yes, because the friend had no reason to know of the collector's meaning and the collector could have avoided the confusion by more careful drafting.
choices.D: Yes, so long as a reasonable person in the friend's position would have considered the letter as referring to the 1987 model.

questions.explanation:
Misunderstanding

A misunderstanding occurs when the parties to a contract attach different meanings to the same term. When a misunderstanding involves a material term, whether a valid contract is formed depends on who knows or has reason to know about the misunderstanding:

  • neither party OR both parties – in which case no contract is formed because there is no meeting of the minds
  • one party – in which case a valid contract is formed, and the unknowing party's meaning of the term controls

Here, the friend accepted the collector's offer to sell the "oldest motorcycle" the collector owned. The friend did not know about the 1985 model (the one the collector intended to sell), and the collector did not know that the friend intended to buy the 1987 model. Since neither party knew nor had reason to know of the other's interpretation of "oldest motorcycle," no contract was formed and the friend is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice A) A party's failure to know or discover facts before entering into a contract—eg, the friend's failure to inquire about the meaning of "oldest motorcycle"—does not qualify as an assumption of the risk that would prevent a party from avoiding a contract due to mistake.

(Choice B — Correct) Neither the friend nor the collector had reason to know of the other's interpretation of "oldest motorcycle," so no contract was formed and the friend is unlikely to prevail.

(Choices C & D) The friend's interpretation of "oldest motorcycle" would control, and the friend would prevail, only if the collector knew or had reason to know of the friend's interpretation. Neither a reasonable person's interpretation nor the collector's ability to avoid the confusion by more careful drafting is relevant.

📌 Educational Objective

If neither (or both) of the parties to a contract know or have reason to know about a misunderstanding involving a material term, no contract is formed. But if one party knows or has reason to know, a valid contract is formed and the unknowing party's meaning of the term controls.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 20 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of misunderstanding)

在这起针对收藏家的违约诉讼中，朋友是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为朋友没有进一步询问“最老的摩托车”这一短语的含义，因此他承担了产生误解的风险。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为朋友和收藏家双方均无理由知道对方对“最老的摩托车”一词的解释。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为朋友无理由知道收藏家的意思，而收藏家本可以通过更谨慎的措辞来避免这种混淆。
zh-choices.D: 会，只要处于朋友立场的理性人会认为信件指的是1987年款的摩托车。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Misunderstanding

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：误解（misunderstanding）下，双方对同一材料术语各有不同理解时，先看谁知道或有理由知道对方的意思；如果双方都不知道，也都不能合理知道，就没有合同。

三秒认题路径：

同词异义 → 材料条款 → 谁知晓 → 都不知晓 → 无合同

核心法律规则

把规则压成考场动作

误解（misunderstanding）是指双方对同一个词用不同意思；考场意思：不是谁更“合理”，而是谁知道或有理由知道（know or have reason to know）对方的理解。

如果是材料条款（material term），且双方都不知道、也都没有理由知道对方的意思，没有合同（no contract），因为没有真正的意思合致。

只有一方知道或有理由知道时，才会形成合同，而且不知情一方（unknowing party）的意思控制结果。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 20 — 这条就是本题的锁定规则：双盲误解，合同不成立。

思维导图

同一个词“oldest motorcycle”
先问：双方是不是给同一材料词塞进了不同意思？
再问：谁知道或有理由知道对方的意思？
本题：友人想买 1987，收藏者想卖 1985，双方都不知对方解读。
卡死点：双方都没“知道或应知”→ 没有意思合致 → 没合同
答案：选 B，友人不能靠 breach of contract 赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：友人没去多问一句，像是自己把风险揽进来了。

但考试真正问的是：这不是“要不要更谨慎”的道德题，而是双方有没有对同一词形成合同意义上的一致理解。

这里看的是“有没有合同”，不是“谁更粗心”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里双方对 oldest motorcycle 各自指向不同车型，且彼此都不知道对方意思，所以没有合同，友人当然难以主张违约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 风险自担误判

✕ A: 把没追问当成 assumed the risk，但本题关键是误解，不是风险承担。

❌ 法律适用 | 知情标准套错

✕ C: 把“友人没理由知道”当成够了；其实要看收藏者是否知道或应知友人的意思。

❌ 事实误判 | 合理人标准偷换

✕ D: 盯着 reasonable person，但误解题不是看抽象理性人，而是看双方知不知道对方意思。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否同词异义，再看双方有没有“知道或有理由知道”，不要被“更合理”的感觉带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：同词异义先看知情，双方都不知就无合同；一方知情，则不知情一方的意思控制。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
The mother of a son and a daughter was dying. The daughter visited her mother in a hospice facility and said, "You know that I have always been the good child, and my brother has always been the bad child. Even so, you have left your property in the will to us 50-50. But it would be really nice if you would sell me the family home for $100,000."
"I don't know," said the mother. "It is worth a lot more than that—at least $250,000."
"That is true," said the daughter. "But I have always been good and visited you, and my brother has never visited you, so that ought to be worth something. And besides, if you won't sell me the house for that price, maybe I won't visit you anymore, either."
"Oh, I wouldn't want that," said the mother, and she signed a contract selling the house to her daughter for $100,000.
Shortly thereafter, the mother died. When her son found out that the house had been sold and was not part of his mother's estate, he sued to have the contract avoided on behalf of the mother.
On what ground would the contract most likely be avoided?

choices.A: Duress.
choices.B: Inadequate consideration.
choices.C: Mistake.
choices.D: Undue influence.

questions.explanation:
A contract induced by undue influence is voidable by the assenting party. Undue influence arises when a party assents to a contract due to unfair or excessive persuasion by someone who dominates or holds a special relationship of trust and confidence with the assenting party. Persuasion is unfair or excessive if it seriously impairs the assenting party's ability to exercise free and competent judgment. The following factors are often considered in making this determination:

  • unfairness of the resulting bargain (eg, sale of home worth $250,000 for $100,000)
  • unavailability of independent advice (eg, attorney unavailable to discuss sale)
  • susceptibility of the assenting party (eg, mental illness, under hospice care)

Here, the daughter held a special relationship of trust with the mother because the daughter was the only child who visited the mother. The daughter's claimed status as the "good child" and her threat to stop visiting likely impaired the mother's judgment and persuaded her to sell her home to the daughter. This is further evidenced by the unfair resulting bargain and the mother's susceptibility. As a result, this contract would most likely be avoided on the ground of undue influence.*

*Had undue influence come from a third party, the assenting party could avoid the contract unless the other contracting party (1) did not know of the undue influence and (2) had given value or relied on the contract in good faith.

(Choice A) Duress arises when a party's assent is induced by physical coercion or an improper threat that leaves no reasonable alternative but to assent or face irreparable harm (not seen here). Therefore, the contract cannot be avoided on this ground.

(Choice B) Adequate consideration exists when, as here, there is a bargained-for exchange of promises or performances. This is true even if that exchange is unequal—eg, $100,000 in exchange for a $250,000 home.

(Choice C) A mistake is a belief not in accord with the facts (eg, had the mother not owned the home) that makes a contract voidable if it concerns a basic assumption on which the contract was made (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A contract is voidable for undue influence when (1) assent stems from unfair or excessive persuasion (2) by someone who dominates or holds a special relationship of trust and confidence with the assenting party.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 177 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (undue influence).
questions.zh-question:
一位有儿子和女儿的母亲快要去世了。女儿在一家临终关怀机构探望母亲时说：“您知道我一直是好孩子，而我哥哥一直是坏孩子。即便如此，您在遗嘱中还是将财产平分给我们。但如果您能以10万美元的价格把家里的房子卖给我，那就太好了。”

“我不知道，”母亲说。“这房子远不止这个价钱——至少值25万美元。”

“没错，”女儿说。“但我一直都很乖，经常来看您，而我哥哥从不来看您，所以这应该值点什么吧。而且，如果您不以这个价格把房子卖给我，或许我以后也不来看您了。”

“哦，我不希望那样，”母亲说，于是她签署了一份合同，以10万美元的价格将房子卖给了女儿。

不久之后，母亲去世了。当儿子发现房子已被出售，并且不属于母亲遗产的一部分时，他代表母亲提起诉讼，要求撤销该合同。

该合同最有可能基于何种理由被撤销？

zh-choices.A: 胁迫。
zh-choices.B: 对价不充分。
zh-choices.C: 错误。
zh-choices.D: 不正当影响。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：一方在信任关系里，用不公平的压力逼对方签明显吃亏的买卖，能不能以 undue influence（不当影响） 让合同可撤销。

三秒认题路径：

信任关系 → 软性施压 → 价差离谱 → 母亲脆弱 → 不当影响

核心法律规则

undue influence（不当影响） 的考场意思：不是硬逼，而是靠 unfair or excessive persuasion（不公平或过度劝说） 让对方失去独立判断。它通常发生在一方 dominates 对方，或者双方有 special relationship of trust and confidence（特殊信任关系） 时。

这题只要看到“照顾者/亲近家人 + 受害方身体或精神脆弱 + 明显吃亏的交易”，就要往不当影响走。voidable（可撤销） 的点在于：受害方是被劝到失去自由判断，不是自己清醒议价。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 177 锁定本题：只要劝说不公平，而且操控者和受害方有信任控制关系，就能撤销合同。

思维导图

先看：这不是普通压价，而是 undue influence（不当影响） 吗？
① 关系女儿长期探视、母亲依赖她 → 信任 / 依赖关系
② 手段“不卖就不来看你” → 软性胁迫，不是物理强迫
③ 结果$100,000 买 价值 $250,000 的房子 → 交易明显失衡
卡死点：母亲在 hospice、判断力弱；不是自己理性谈价，而是被亲近者拿情感压力推着签字。
结论合同可因 undue influence 被撤销 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：女儿说“你不卖我就不来看你”，这听起来像 duress（胁迫）。

但考试真正问的是：这里没有物理强迫，也不是逼到“别无选择”的那种硬胁迫，而是利用亲情和依赖关系慢慢压住母亲的判断。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 hospice facility、明显低价和“不给探视就不卖”的话，正好对应 unfair or excessive persuasion 加上信任依赖关系，所以合同最可能因不当影响被撤销。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 这里是情感施压，不是逼到没有退路的 physical coercion。

❌ 法律适用 | 价格低廉误判

✕ B: 价差再大也只是吃亏，不自动变成无对价。

❌ 事实误判 | 基础事实偷换

✕ C: 题目没说母亲搞错房子归属，别把 mistake 硬塞进来。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找关系，再看施压方式，最后盯住交易是否明显失衡。

考场速记

记住：undue influence（不当影响） = trust + pressure + unfair deal。看到“照顾关系、情感绑架、脆弱当事人、离谱低价”，先想它；看到硬逼、暴力或真没退路，才去想 duress（胁迫）。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A developer contracted in writing with a buyer to sell a house on a one-acre lot for $100,000. The developer told the buyer that the lot abutted a national park and that the water for the house came from a natural artesian spring. The developer knew that both these representations were important to the buyer and that both were false. The buyer moved into the house and eight months later learned that a private golf course was being constructed on the adjacent land and that the water for the house came from the city reservoir. The buyer immediately sued the developer to avoid the contract. The construction of the golf course will probably increase the market value of the buyer's property, and the water from the city reservoir exceeds all established standards for drinking water.
Is the buyer likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because eight months exceeds a reasonable time for contract avoidance.
choices.B: No, because the developer's misstatements caused no economic harm to the buyer.
choices.C: Yes, because the buyer retained the power to avoid the contract due to fraud.
choices.D: Yes, because the contract was void ab initio.

questions.explanation:
Factors used to determine reasonable time to avoid contract

Extent to which:

  • delay enabled (or might have enabled) party with power of avoidance to speculate at other party's risk
  • delay resulted (or might have resulted) in justifiable reliance by other party or third party
  • ground for avoidance was result of either party's fault
  • other party's conduct contributed to delay

Misrepresentation is a defense to enforceability that makes a contract voidable by the adversely affected party. This defense is available when:

  • the misrepresentation was fraudulent (ie, made knowingly or recklessly with intent to induce the other party's assent to the contract) OR material (ie, likely to induce a reasonable person's assent)
  • the misrepresentation induced assent to the contract and
  • the adversely affected party justifiably relied on the misrepresentation.

If the misrepresentation was fraudulent, then the adversely affected party must seek to avoid the contract within a reasonable time after learning of the misrepresentation.* Otherwise, the power to avoid the contract is lost.

Here, the developer fraudulently misrepresented both the location of the lot and the water source, which induced the buyer to purchase the house. Because the developer's statements were not obviously false, the buyer justifiably relied on them. And since the buyer immediately sued the developer to avoid the contract after discovering the misrepresentation eight months later, the buyer retained the power to avoid the contract and will likely prevail (Choice A).

*If the misrepresentation was nonfraudulent, then the reasonable time period begins to run when the party knows or has reason to know about the misrepresentation.

(Choice B) A party may avoid a contract for misrepresentation even if the resulting contract causes that party no economic harm.

(Choice D) The contract was not void ab initio (ie, invalid from the outset). Rather, it was voidable, meaning that it operated as a valid contract until the buyer took steps to avoid it.

📌 Educational Objective

To avoid a contract for fraudulent misrepresentation, the adversely affected party must seek this remedy within a reasonable time after learning of the misrepresentation.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when misrepresentation makes a contract voidable).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 381 cmt. b (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when power to avoid contract is lost due to delay).
