questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In order to raise revenue, a city required home-repair contractors who performed work within the city limits to pay a licensing fee to a city agency. A contractor who was unaware of the fee requirement agreed to perform home repairs for a city resident. After the contractor completed the work, the resident discovered that the contractor had not paid the licensing fee, and she refused to pay for the repairs, which were otherwise satisfactory.
If the contractor sues the resident for breach of contract, how is the court likely to rule?

choices.A: Although the contract violates the law and is void, the court will require the homeowner to pay the contractor the reasonable value of the work accepted.
choices.B: Although the contract violates the law, the court will find that public policy does not bar enforcement of the contract, because the purpose of the fee is merely to raise revenue.
choices.C: Because the contract violates the law and is void, the court will not enforce it.
choices.D: Because the purpose of the fee is merely to raise revenue, the court will find that the contract does not violate the law but will allow the contractor to recover his costs only.

questions.explanation:
Weighing public policy v. Interest in enforcing illegal contract
Public policy Interest in enforcing
  • Strength of policy as shown by legislature or courts
  • Likelihood nonenforcement will further policy
  • Seriousness and/or deliberateness of misconduct
  • Connection between misconduct & contract
  • Parties' justified expectations
  • Forfeiture that would result from nonenforcement
  • Special public interest in enforcement

Illegal contracts are generally void as against public policy. But if a contract is illegal solely because a party does not have a required license, then the enforceability of the contract depends on whether the purpose behind the licensing requirement is:

  • economic (eg, raise revenue) – in which case the contract is enforceable or
  • regulatory (eg, protect public health or safety) – in which case the contract is unenforceable if the public policy behind the requirement clearly outweighs the interest in enforcing the contract.

Here, the contract between the contractor and resident was illegal because the contractor had not paid the required licensing fee to the city agency. But since the purpose of this fee is merely to raise revenue for the city, the court will likely find that public policy does not bar enforcement of the contract (Choice C).

(Choice A) Had the contract been void on public-policy grounds, then the court may have required the homeowner to pay restitution damages (ie, the reasonable value of the work accepted) to avoid unjust enrichment.

(Choice D) The contract does violate the law. But public policy does not bar its enforcement, and the contractor is entitled to recover the full contract price—not his costs only.

📌 Educational Objective

When a party does not have a required license, the enforceability of the contract depends on whether the purpose behind the requirement is (1) economic, in which case the contract is enforceable, or (2) regulatory, in which case it is unenforceable if the public policy behind the requirement clearly outweighs the interest in enforcement.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 181 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when failure to comply with licensing requirement makes contract unenforceable).
questions.zh-question:
为了增加财政收入，某市要求在该市范围内施工的家居维修承包商向市级机构支付一笔执照费。一名承包商不知道此项费用要求，同意为一位市里的居民进行家居维修。承包商完工后，该居民发现承包商没有支付执照费，因此拒绝支付维修费用，尽管维修工作在其他方面是令人满意的。

如果承包商以违约为由起诉该居民，法院可能会如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 虽然合同违法且无效，但法院将要求房主向承包商支付其已接受工作的合理价值。
zh-choices.B: 虽然合同违法，但法院会认定公共政策并不禁止执行该合同，因为该费用的目的仅仅是为了增加财政收入。
zh-choices.C: 因为合同违法且无效，法院将不会执行该合同。
zh-choices.D: 因为该费用的目的仅仅是为了增加财政收入，法院将认定该合同不违法，但只允许承包商收回其成本。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to Enforcement

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：无牌照或未缴许可费导致的合同违法，是否因为许可目的只是筹集收入（raise revenue）而仍可执行。

三秒认题路径：

许可费未缴 → 合同违法 → 看目的 → 纯收入型 → 仍可执行

核心法律规则

只抓决定答案的规则

一般来说，违法合同会因公共政策（public policy）而不能执行。可如果合同之所以违法，只是因为一方没拿到必要执照，考试就要先问：这个执照要求的目的，是不是只是经济性的。

如果目的只是筹集收入（raise revenue），那合同通常还是可执行；如果目的是监管、保护公众健康或安全，就要再看公共政策是否明显大于执行合同的利益。这里的许可费只是给城市创收，所以不挡执行。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 181 — 没有遵守许可要求时，先看该要求是经济性还是监管性，再决定合同能不能执行。

思维导图

先问：这份合同为什么“违法”？
如果只是没缴许可费
再问：许可要求的目的是什么？
经济性 / raise revenue
结论：通常仍可执行，城市不能靠“违法”直接赖账。
监管性 / 保护健康安全
再比重：若公共政策明显更强，才不执行。
本题事实锚点
题干已给：license fee 只是给城市raise revenue
所以答案：B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 contractor 没付费，合同就一定void，法院只能帮 homeowner 赖掉付款。

但考试真正问的是：这个许可要求到底是为了管人，还是只是为了收钱；前者才更可能挡住执行，后者通常不挡。

你要盯的是“许可制度的目的”，不是看到“违法”两个字就直接判死刑。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 licensing fee 只是为城市筹集收入，所以虽然合同违法，public policy 仍不会阻止执行，contractor 可以按合同价主张付款。

❌ 概念混淆 | 不当恢复误判

✕ A: 把“合同无效”当成一定能拿到 restitution，但本题没走到那一步。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对无效误判

✕ C: 看到没执照就直接判 void，忽略了许可目的只是创收。

❌ 事实误判 | 成本救济偷换

✕ D: 把“可执行”偷换成只赔 costs only，题干没有这个限制。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓许可制度目的，再决定公共政策是否真的挡住合同执行。

考场速记

记住一句：“看许可目的，不看表面违法。” 许可只是 raise revenue 时，通常还是能执行合同；只有监管型许可被公共政策压过时，才真可能挡住。

question_analysis.skill_tested: distinguish revenue-raising from regulatory licensing for contract enforceability

reason.en: Determines whether the licensing statute is regulatory (voids contract) or merely revenue-raising (contract remains enforceable).
reason.zh: 决定该许可法规是监管性（合同无效）还是仅为筹款（合同仍可执行）。

reason.en: The type of licensing requirement (regulatory vs. revenue) is the pivotal legal distinction in this question.
reason.zh: 许可要求的类型（监管性与筹款性）是本题的核心法律区别。

reason.en: Good-faith ignorance supports the argument that the contractor should not be barred from recovery on public policy grounds.
reason.zh: 善意不知情支持承包商不应因公共政策而被拒绝追偿的论点。

reason.en: The work was properly done; denying recovery would unjustly enrich the resident without any public protection rationale.
reason.zh: 工程已妥善完成；拒绝追偿将不公平地使居民获益，且无任何公共保护依据。

reason.en: The contractor is seeking enforcement of the contract; the court must decide whether the licensing violation bars this remedy.
reason.zh: 承包商寻求合同执行；法院须决定许可违规是否阻止该救济。

reason.en: Incorrectly treats a revenue-raising license violation as voiding the contract; regulatory licenses void contracts, not revenue licenses.
reason.zh: 错误地将筹款许可违规视为使合同无效；监管性许可才能使合同无效，筹款许可不能。

A.text: reasonable value of the work accepted

reason.en: Offers a restitution remedy as a fallback when contract is void—but the premise (void contract) is incorrect here.
reason.zh: 当合同无效时提供返还救济作为替代方案——但前提（合同无效）在此不正确。

B.text: public policy does not bar enforcement

label.zh: 公共政策对违法性的例外

reason.en: The correct legal conclusion: courts enforce contracts where the licensing statute serves only a revenue purpose, not a protective one.
reason.zh: 正确的法律结论：当许可法规仅服务于筹款目的而非保护目的时，法院将执行合同。

reason.en: This phrase identifies the statute's purpose and triggers the rule that such licenses do not bar contract enforcement.
reason.zh: 此短语识别法规的目的，并触发此类许可不阻止合同执行的规则。

C.text: violates the law and is void

reason.en: Applies the regulatory-license rule where the revenue-raising exception should apply; the strongest distractor for students who conflate all licensing statutes.
reason.zh: 在应适用筹款例外规则时，错误地适用监管许可规则；对混淆所有许可法规的学生来说是最强的干扰项。

reason.en: The categorical non-enforcement rule only applies to regulatory (protective) licensing statutes, not revenue-raising ones.
reason.zh: 一律不执行的规则仅适用于监管性（保护性）许可法规，而非筹款性许可。

reason.en: Incorrect premise: the contract does technically violate the ordinance; the correct analysis is that despite the violation, policy allows enforcement.
reason.zh: 错误前提：合同在技术上确实违反了条例；正确分析是尽管存在违规，政策仍允许执行。

reason.en: Invents an unsupported damages limitation; if the contract is enforceable, the contractor recovers the agreed contract price, not merely costs.
reason.zh: 捏造了无依据的损害赔偿限制；若合同可执行，承包商应回收约定合同价格，而非仅限成本。

highlights.text: In order to raise revenue

reason.en: The entire legal outcome turns on this phrase: a fee imposed solely to raise revenue does not make the underlying contract void or unenforceable as against public policy.
reason.zh: 整个法律结果取决于此短语：仅为筹款而征收的费用不会使基础合同因违反公共政策而无效或不可执行。

highlights.text: contractor who was unaware of the fee requirement

label.zh: 对许可要求的善意不知情

reason.en: The contractor's innocent non-compliance further supports enforcement; there is no element of fraud or harm to the public to justify denying recovery.
reason.zh: 承包商的善意不合规进一步支持合同执行；不存在欺诈或危害公众的因素来证明拒绝追偿是合理的。

highlights.text: the repairs, which were otherwise satisfactory

label.zh: 无牌承包商的令人满意的履行

reason.en: Confirms the work was properly performed; denying recovery under a revenue-raising statute would unjustly enrich the resident without any protective rationale.
reason.zh: 确认工程已妥善完成；在筹款法规下拒绝追偿将不公平地使居民获益，且无任何保护性依据。

highlights.text: how is the court likely to rule

reason.en: Frames the question as requiring selection of the correct legal outcome, not merely identification of a rule; students must apply the revenue vs. regulatory distinction to a specific result.
reason.zh: 将问题定位为需要选择正确的法律结果，而非仅识别规则；学生必须将筹款与监管的区别应用于具体结果。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A man who wanted to sell his home executed a written listing agreement with a real estate broker. The agreement was signed by both parties and gave the broker the exclusive right to sell the home for 60 days. It also gave her the right to receive a commission for up to 30 days after the exclusivity period had terminated if the home sold to a buyer with whom the broker had negotiated during the exclusivity period. A clause in the agreement provided that any modifications must be in writing.
Two weeks later, the parties orally agreed to extend the exclusivity period by 60 days (for a total of 120 days). The 120-day exclusivity period ended without a sale. Twenty days later, a buyer with whom the broker had negotiated while the exclusivity period was still in force offered to purchase the home. The man accepted the offer and concluded the sale but refused to pay the broker a commission.
If the broker sues the man for breach of contract, will she be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the parties waived the right to modify the written agreement.
choices.B: No, because the parol evidence rule will prevent proof of the parties' oral agreement.
choices.C: Yes, because the original agreement is not subject to the statute of frauds.
choices.D: Yes, because the parties' oral agreement was an effective modification of their written agreement.

questions.explanation:
"No oral modification" (NOM) clause
Common law (contracts for services or real estate)
  • NOM clause enforceable only if modification must be in writing under statute of frauds
UCC (contracts for sale of goods)
  • All parties are merchants – NOM clause always enforceable
  • ≥ 1 party is nonmerchant – NOM clause in merchant's form must be separately signed by nonmerchant(s) to be enforceable
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

At common law, a prior written contract can be modified by a subsequent oral agreement unless the modified contract falls within the statute of frauds. This is true even if the written contract contains a "no oral modification" (NOM) clause purporting to require that any modification be in writing (Choice A). That is because of the common-law principle that the parties to a contract should not be deterred from changing their minds. However, any modification (oral or written) must still be supported by consideration to be enforceable.

Here, the parties orally agreed to extend the exclusivity period by 60 days. Although the written agreement contained a NOM clause, the modified exclusivity period did not need to be evidenced by a writing since no statute of frauds provision applies.* And since there was consideration—60 more days of exclusivity in exchange for 60 more days of service—the parties' oral agreement effectively modified their written agreement.

The terms of the modified contract are found partly in the original written agreement and partly in the modifying oral agreement. As a result, the broker had the right to receive a commission for up to 30 days after the 120-day exclusivity period had ended if the home sold to a buyer with whom she had negotiated during that period—which it did. Therefore, the broker will likely prevail.

*Contracts to pay a real estate broker a commission ordinarily fall outside the land-contract provision of the statute of frauds. Some jurisdictions have added a provision to their statute of frauds requiring such contracts to be in writing, but that is not the case here.

(Choice B) The parol evidence rule generally prevents proof of prior or contemporaneous agreements that modify or contradict the terms of a written contract. But this rule does not prevent proof of subsequent agreements between the parties—eg, the oral agreement entered after the written listing agreement was executed.

(Choice C) The agreement to pay the real estate broker a commission is not subject to the statute of frauds. Nevertheless, the broker can only prevail if the oral modification agreement also falls outside of the statute of frauds.

📌 Educational Objective

Common law ignores "no oral modification" clauses and allows written contracts to be modified by subsequent oral agreements unless the modified contract falls within the statute of frauds.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 149 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (oral modifications).
questions.zh-question:
一名想出售其房屋的男子与一名房地产经纪人签订了一份书面委托销售协议。该协议由双方签署，并授予经纪人在60天内独家销售该房屋的权利。协议还规定，如果在独家销售期结束后30天内，房屋出售给经纪人在独家销售期内曾进行过谈判的买家，经纪人有权收取佣金。协议中的一项条款规定，任何修改都必须以书面形式进行。

两周后，双方口头同意将独家销售期延长60天（总计120天）。120天的独家销售期结束时，房屋并未售出。二十天后，一名经纪人在独家销售期内曾与之谈判过的买家要约购买该房屋。该男子接受了要约并完成了交易，但拒绝向经纪人支付佣金。

如果经纪人以违约为由起诉该男子，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为有效修改原始协议需要新的对价。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为口头证据规则（parol evidence rule）将阻止对双方口头协议的证明。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为原始协议不受《欺诈法》（statute of frauds）的约束。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为双方的口头协议是对其书面协议的有效修改。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法（common law）下，书面合同里的禁止口头修改条款（no oral modification clause, NOM clause）通常不挡住后来的口头修改，只要修改不落入防欺诈法（statute of frauds），而且还有对价。

三秒认题路径：

书面合同 → 口头延期 → 不进SOF → 有对价 → 口头修改有效

核心法律规则

普通法（common law）下，先前的书面合同可以被后来的口头协议修改；禁止口头修改条款（NOM clause）一般不自动封死这条路。考场意思：你不能只看到“必须书面修改”就停下，还要先问这次修改有没有撞上防欺诈法（statute of frauds）。

如果修改后的内容本来就不需要书面形式，而且修改有对价（consideration），那口头修改就可能有效。这里就是“再给 60 天独家销售权，换 60 天额外服务”，所以修改生效。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 149（oral modifications）——它锁定了“普通法下后来的口头修改可成立，只要不被防欺诈法拦住”。

思维导图

先问：这题在卡什么？
1.先看是不是最终判决（final judgment）？这题不是程序上诉题，而是合同修改题。
2.再看有没有必须书面的防欺诈法（statute of frauds）要求？本题没有。
3.再看NOM clause能不能挡住口头修改？普通法下通常不能。
4.卡死点：有对价 + 不进SOF = 口头延期有效
5.结论：120 天独家期成立，买家在保护期内出现，佣金应付，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：合同都写了“必须书面修改（must be in writing）”，那口头延期当然无效。

但考试真正问的是：普通法下，后来双方自己改主意的口头修改（oral modification），只要没有被防欺诈法卡住，通常还是能成立。

命题人想骗你把“写了不得口头改”当成绝对规则；实际上，普通法更看重后来的真实一致意思和对价。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的口头延长 60 天有对价，而且这类经纪佣金安排通常不受防欺诈法（statute of frauds）约束，所以口头修改有效。

❌ 概念混淆 | NOM绝对化

✕ A: 把no oral modification当成绝对封口，忘了普通法允许后改。

❌ 法律适用 | 事后协议误伤

✕ B: 把后来的口头延长误塞进parol evidence rule，它管的不是这种后续修改。

❌ 事实误判 | SOF偷换场景

✕ C: 盯着statute of frauds就说能赢，但本题的经纪佣金协议通常不需要书面。

这题建议用什么方法？

先查后改协议是不是新事实，再问 SOF 和对价，别被“必须书面”四个字直接带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：普通法下，NOM clause 不是铁门，后来的口头修改只要不撞上防欺诈法，再加上对价，通常就能改成。

这题的快捷法：先问“改的是不是后来发生的事”，再问“有没有 SOF”，最后问“有没有对价”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply common law rule that NOM clauses are themselves waivable

keywords.text: any modifications must be in writing

reason.en: Tests whether this clause absolutely bars oral modifications or can itself be waived.
reason.zh: 考查该条款是否绝对禁止口头修改，或其自身能否被放弃。

keywords.text: orally agreed to extend the exclusivity period

reason.en: A subsequent oral agreement can waive a written-modification requirement under common law.
reason.zh: 在普通法下，后续口头协议可放弃书面修改要求。

reason.en: Defines the time period governing broker's commission rights; oral extension directly affects it.
reason.zh: 决定经纪人佣金权利的时间窗口，口头延长直接影响其效力。

reason.en: The post-expiry commission clause only applies to buyers the broker dealt with during the (now extended) period.
reason.zh: 到期后佣金条款仅适用于在（现已延长的）独家期间内接触的买家。

keywords.text: broker sues the man for breach of contract

reason.en: Frames the legal question as whether the oral modification is enforceable so as to support a breach claim.
reason.zh: 将法律问题框定为口头修改是否可执行，以支持违约主张。

reason.en: Confuses the concept: parties waived the NOM clause, not the right to modify; the modification itself is valid.
reason.zh: 混淆概念：当事人放弃的是书面修改要求，而非修改权本身。

reason.en: The parol evidence rule bars prior/contemporaneous extrinsic evidence; it does not bar evidence of subsequent oral modifications.
reason.zh: 口头证据规则排除先前或同时的外部证据，但不排除后续口头修改的证据。

C.text: not subject to the statute of frauds

reason.en: While listing agreements may not require writing under the SOF, this is not the reason the broker prevails; the oral modification's validity is the operative reason.
reason.zh: 虽然挂牌协议未必须书面，但这不是经纪人胜诉的原因；口头修改的效力才是关键。

D.text: oral agreement was an effective modification

reason.en: Correctly states the common law rule: a NOM clause can be waived by a later oral agreement between the parties.
reason.zh: 正确陈述普通法规则：书面修改条款可被当事人后续的口头协议所放弃。

highlights.text: any modifications must be in writing

reason.en: The central trap: test-takers assume this clause makes the oral extension void, but common law allows parties to orally waive even this requirement.
reason.zh: 核心陷阱：考生易认为该条款使口头延期无效，但普通法允许当事人以口头方式放弃该要求。

highlights.text: orally agreed to extend the exclusivity period by 60 days

reason.en: This act constitutes a valid waiver of the NOM clause and extends the exclusivity period to 120 days.
reason.zh: 此行为构成对书面修改条款的有效放弃，并将独家期延长至120天。

highlights.text: a buyer with whom the broker had negotiated while the exclusivity period was still in force

label.zh: 延长期内的佣金触发事件

reason.en: Because the oral extension is valid, this buyer falls within the 30-day post-exclusivity commission window, entitling the broker to her commission.
reason.zh: 由于口头延长有效，该买家在独家期届满后30天佣金窗口内，经纪人有权收取佣金。

highlights.text: refused to pay the broker a commission

reason.en: Identifies the specific contractual breach at issue once the oral modification is deemed enforceable.
reason.zh: 一旦口头修改被认定可执行，即确定了所诉的具体合同违约行为。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A husband lost his job and decided to borrow money against his marital home. Each time he applied for a mortgage, his wife contacted the lender and withdrew the mortgage application. One Saturday evening, the husband forced the wife to sit at the kitchen table and placed a mortgage application in front of her. As he waved a large pair of scissors in front of the wife's face, he demanded that she promise to sign the application by the end of the week. The wife, frightened by her husband, agreed to do so. On Monday morning, the wife went to a notary public's office alone and signed the application. The notary asked the wife if she signed the application of her own free will, and the wife replied, "It is what it is." Several months later, the mortgage went into default.
Does the lender have a breach-of-contract claim against the wife?

choices.A: No, because the husband physically compelled the wife to sign the mortgage application.
choices.B: No, because the husband threatened the wife with serious bodily harm.
choices.C: Yes, because the wife never voided the contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the wife was no longer under duress when she signed the mortgage application.

questions.explanation:
Duress is a defense to contract enforceability when a party was induced to assent by any of the following:

  • Physical compulsion – rendering the contract void if the party’s assent was compelled by physical force OR imminent threat of death or serious bodily harm
  • Improper threat by contracting party – rendering the contract voidable by the threatened party if he/she had no reasonable alternative but to succumb to the improper threat
  • Improper threat by third party – rendering the contract voidable by the threatened party if he/she had no choice but to succumb to the third party’s improper threat (not seen here), unless the other contracting party did not know of the duress AND relied on the contract in good faith

Here, the wife manifested her assent to the contract by signing the mortgage application. The husband did not physically compel her to do so—eg, by grabbing her hand and using it to sign (Choice A). And though waving scissors in front of the wife’s face on Saturday may have threatened serious bodily harm, that threat was no longer imminent when she signed the application on Monday (Choice B). Therefore, duress is no defense, and the lender has a breach-of-contract claim against the wife.

(Choice C) A contract may be voidable in certain situations, none of which are seen here. Therefore, the wife could not have voided the contract after willingly signing it.

📌 Educational Objective

Duress occurs when a party’s assent to a contract is compelled by physical force or imminent threat of death or serious bodily harm. Duress also occurs when a party receives an improper threat and has no reasonable alternative but to succumb.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 174–176 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (discussing duress caused by physical compulsion and improper threat).
questions.zh-question:
一位丈夫失业后，决定用其婚内住宅作抵押借款。每当他申请抵押贷款时，他的妻子都会联系贷款人并撤回抵押贷款申请。一个周六的晚上，丈夫强迫妻子坐在厨房的餐桌旁，并将一份抵押贷款申请书放在她面前。他一边在妻子面前挥舞着一把大剪刀，一边要求她承诺在本周末前签署该申请书。妻子因受丈夫惊吓，同意了这一要求。周一早上，妻子独自前往公证处签署了该申请书。公证员问妻子是否是出于自愿签署该申请书，妻子回答说：“事已至此，就这样吧。”几个月后，该抵押贷款出现违约。

贷款人是否可以对妻子提起违约之诉？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为丈夫以物理胁迫的方式强迫妻子签署抵押贷款申请书。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为丈夫以严重的身体伤害威胁妻子。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为妻子从未宣告该合同无效。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为当妻子签署抵押贷款申请书时，她已不再处于胁迫之下。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：胁迫（duress）能不能让妻子对按揭申请免责；关键看她签字时是不是还处在即时的威胁之下。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否终局威胁 → 再看签字时点 → 还是即时威胁吗 → 不能即上诉式逃避 → 选能主张合同成立

核心法律规则

胁迫（duress）是合同可执行性的抗辩。身体强制（physical compulsion），或者对死亡/严重人身伤害的即时威胁（imminent threat），才会直接把同意击穿。

如果只是早先被吓到，但后来在没有当场刀架脖子、没有当场强迫签字的情况下自己去签，考试通常会说：no duress at signing，所以合同仍可被执行。

本题里，真正看的是妻子周一独自去公证处签字这一刻；周六挥剪刀的恐吓已经不是即时威胁了，所以贷款人可以对她主张违约。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 174–176 的规则锁定本题：只有身体强制或即时严重伤害威胁，才足以构成胁迫。

思维导图

先问：签字时还有没有“当场逼签”或“即时严重伤害威胁”？
YES如果真是当场按手签字、或者刀已经贴脸 → 合同可能因胁迫而不可执行
NO如果只是前一晚被吓到，第二天自己去签 → 继续看
再问：威胁在签字当下是否仍然“即时”可怕到没有正常选择？
NO周六的剪刀威胁已过去，周一签字时不再是即时威胁
结论：胁迫抗辩失败，贷款人可对妻子主张违约。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：丈夫周六拿剪刀吓人，听起来已经很可怕，所以妻子一定能躲掉合同责任。

但考试真正问的是：签字那一刻有没有还活着的即时威胁（imminent threat），而不是前一天晚上有多吓人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题里更准确地说，是看签字时还有没有真正的强迫。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最关键的 周一独自签字 说明威胁已不再即时；她当时不是被当场逼签，所以丈夫先前的恐吓不能让合同自动失效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 物理强制误判

✕ A: 把“被吓到”当成physical compulsion，但题干没有人抓着她的手硬签。

❌ 事实误判 | 即时性偷换

✕ B: 只看到周六威胁，忽略周一签字时威胁已不再imminent。

❌ 法律适用 | 可撤销误判

✕ C: 以为“没去撤销”就当然输，但这里根本先要过胁迫门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定签字时点，再抓“即时威胁”门槛，别被前情恐吓带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：No imminent threat at signing, no duress. 先看签字当下有没有真强迫；没有，就别把早先威胁误当成免责理由。

这题就记一条：周六吓人，不等于周一还能取消合同。

question_analysis.skill_tested: determine applicability of contract duress defense

keywords.text: waved a large pair of scissors

reason.en: Establishes the husband's initial threat of force.
reason.zh: 确立了丈夫最初的暴力威胁事实。

reason.en: Indicates the initial subjective effect of the threat on the wife's state of mind.
reason.zh: 表明该威胁最初对妻子心理状态的主观影响。

keywords.text: went to a notary public's office alone

reason.en: Indicates she was no longer in a coercive environment when executing the contract.
reason.zh: 表明她在签署合同时已脱离了受胁迫的环境。

reason.en: The exact moment of contract execution when voluntariness is evaluated.
reason.zh: 评估自愿性的合意达成关键时刻。

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests the threat constituted physical compulsion (making the contract void) rather than a threat (making it voidable).
reason.zh: 错误地暗示威胁构成了物理强迫（导致合同无效），而非普通的胁迫威胁（导致合同可撤销）。

B.text: threatened the wife with serious bodily harm

reason.en: Focuses on the threat on Saturday rather than the state of mind when signing on Monday.
reason.zh: 将注意力吸引在周六发生的威胁上，而非周一签署合意时的心理状态。

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes the contract was voidable but not voided, when in fact duress was not present at execution.
reason.zh: 错误地假设合同本是可撤销但未撤销，而实际上签署时并不存在强迫状态。

reason.en: Correctly identifies that duress must be active at the moment of execution to defense the contract.
reason.zh: 正确指出强迫必须在合同签署那一刻依然有效，才能作为合同抗辩。

highlights.text: As he waved a large pair of scissors in front of the wife's face, he demanded that she promise to sign the application by the end of the week.

reason.en: Triggers the rule on duress by threat of physical harm.
reason.zh: 触发有关通过人身伤害威胁实施强迫的规则。

highlights.text: On Monday morning, the wife went to a notary public's office alone and signed the application.

reason.en: Shows she was no longer under duress when she actually signed, defeating the defense.
reason.zh: 表明她实际签署合同时已不再处于强迫状态，从而击败该抗辩。

highlights.text: Does the lender have a breach-of-contract claim against the wife?

label.en: enforceability of contract under duress defense
label.zh: 强迫抗辩下的合同效力

reason.en: The core question asking whether the signed agreement is enforceable against the wife.
reason.zh: 核心提问，要求判断所签署协议对妻子是否具有执行力。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
During negotiations to purchase a used car, a buyer asked a dealer whether the car had ever been in an accident. The dealer replied: "It is a fine car and has been thoroughly inspected and comes with a certificate of assured quality. Feel free to have the car inspected by your own mechanic." In actuality, the car had been in a major accident, and the dealer had repaired and repainted the car, successfully concealing evidence of the accident. The buyer declined to have the car inspected by his own mechanic, explaining that he would rely on the dealer's certificate of assured quality. At no time did the dealer disclose that the car had previously been in an accident. The parties then signed a contract of sale. After the car was delivered and paid for, the buyer learned that the car had been in a major accident.
If the buyer sues the dealer to rescind the transaction, is the buyer likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because the buyer had the opportunity to have the car inspected by his own mechanic and declined to do so.
choices.B: No, because the dealer did not affirmatively assert that the car had not been in an accident.
choices.C: Yes, because the contract was unconscionable.
choices.D: Yes, because the dealer's statement was intentionally misleading and the dealer concealed evidence of the accident.

questions.explanation:
Misrepresentation is an untrue assertion of fact often made in an affirmative statement. It can also be asserted through conduct—ie, an act of concealment intended to prevent discovery of facts or nondisclosure ((Choice B)). When either form of misrepresentation occurs, a contract is voidable and can be rescinded by the adversely affected party if:

  • the misrepresentation was fraudulent (ie, made knowingly or recklessly with intent to induce the other party's assent to the contract) OR material (ie, likely to induce a reasonable person's assent)
  • the misrepresentation induced assent to the contract and
  • the adversely affected party justifiably relied* on the misrepresentation.

Here, the dealer repaired and repainted the car to conceal accident damage. This fraudulent misrepresentation, along with the dealer's misleading statements about the car's history, induced the buyer to purchase the car. And since the dealer's misrepresentations were not obviously false (eg, had the accident damage been visible) or known by the buyer to be false, he justifiably relied on them. Therefore, his action to rescind the contract is likely to succeed.

*This element is met unless the misrepresentation was patently and obviously false or the adversely affected party knew that it was false.

(Choice A) The buyer's failure to have the car inspected by his own mechanic does not make his reliance on the dealer's misrepresentations unjustified or prevent him from rescinding the contract.

(Choice C) A contract is unconscionable when (1) the contract terms are one-sided or create unfair surprise or (2) the bargaining process provides no meaningful choice to a party (neither of which is seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A contract is voidable for misrepresentation if (1) the misrepresentation was fraudulent or material, (2) it induced assent to the contract, and (3) the adversely affected party justifiably relied on it.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when misrepresentation makes a contract voidable).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 168–72 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when reliance on assertions of fact or opinion is justified).
questions.zh-question:
在一场二手车购买谈判中，一名买家询问经销商该车是否曾发生过事故。经销商回答说：“这是一辆好车，已经过全面检查，并附有质量保证证书。您可以随时请您自己的技师检查这辆车。”实际上，该车曾发生过一次重大事故，经销商修理并重新喷漆，成功地掩盖了事故的证据。买家拒绝让自己的技师检查该车，并解释说他将信赖经销商的质量保证证书。经销商自始至终没有披露该车曾发生过事故。随后，双方签署了一份销售合同。车辆交付并付款后，买家得知该车曾发生过重大事故。

如果买家起诉经销商要求撤销该交易，买家是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为买家有机会让自己的技师检查车辆，但他拒绝了。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为经销商并未明确断言该车没有发生过事故。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该合同不合情理。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为经销商的陈述具有故意误导性，并且经销商隐瞒了事故的证据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖方用 故意误导（fraudulent misrepresentation） 和 隐瞒（concealment / nondisclosure） 骗买家签约后，买家能否解除合同。

三秒认题路径：

隐瞒事故 → 虚假陈述 → 诱导签约 → 依赖成立 → 可撤销

核心法律规则

虚假陈述（misrepresentation） 不只包括明说假话，也包括故意隐瞒事实、让对方看不见真相。考试上只要这类误导是 fraudulent（欺诈性） 或 material（重要），而且真的诱导了对方签约，对方又 justifiably relied（考场意思：这种依赖算数），合同就可以被 rescinded（撤销）。

这里卖家把事故修复并重新喷漆，目的就是 concealment（故意遮掩）；再加上他讲了会让人误信车况的说法，已经够构成可撤销的误导。买家没找自己技师验车，不会自动把依赖变成不合理。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 和 §§ 168–72 锁定本题结论：欺诈或重大误导致使对方同意的，合同可撤销。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 虚假陈述（misrepresentation）？
是 故意隐瞒事故
修复+喷漆遮痕 → 误导对方相信
车况良好 → 诱导签约
买家付款提车
再查 能否说“终局后再救济”在本题不成立？不能，这题不是要等到以后才看。
最后 买家可撤销
答案选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：买家既然没让自己机械师检查，就像是自己放弃了保护。
但考试真正问的是：卖家有没有用 欺骗性隐瞒（concealment） 把真相藏起来，让买家在误信下签约。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

也就是说，买家是否有机会自行验车，只是背景；真正卡分的是卖家有没有故意误导、买家有没有合理依赖。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 repaired and repainted 说明卖家主动遮掩事故痕迹，再配合误导性说法，已经构成可撤销的欺诈性误导。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略遮掩

✕ A: 把 declined 验车当成放弃救济，但卖家先前已在隐瞒事故。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只盯明说

✕ B: 只认“没明说没事故”，却漏掉 concealment 也算误导。

❌ 法律适用 | 错套合同瑕疵

✕ C: 把这题硬拽成 unconscionable，但这里问的是误导，不是条款压迫。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有故意隐瞒”，再看“是否诱导签约”，不要被买家没验车这条噪音带跑。

考场速记

记住一句话：故意隐瞒 + 诱导签约 + 真实依赖，就可能让合同可撤销。

遇到卖家把缺陷修掉、喷掉、藏掉这种题，先想 misrepresentation，再想买家有没有 justifiable reliance。

question_analysis.skill_tested: determining contract voidability for fraudulent concealment

reason.en: Indicates active conduct to hide a defect, which constitutes an assertion that the defect does not exist.
reason.zh: 表明主动隐瞒缺陷的行为，这在法律上等同于主张该缺陷不存在。

keywords.text: rely on the dealer's certificate of assured quality

reason.en: Shows that the buyer's assent was induced by and relied on the dealer's representations.
reason.zh: 表明买方的同意是由车商的陈述所引导并产生信赖的。

reason.en: The specific remedy sought, requiring proof of fraudulent or material misrepresentation.
reason.zh: 寻求的特定救济，要求证明存在欺诈性或实质性的虚假陈述。

reason.en: Relates to whether a passive failure to speak can support rescission alongside active concealment.
reason.zh: 关系到消极的不作为（未说明）是否能与积极隐瞒一同支持合同解除。

A.text: opportunity to have the car inspected

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests that failing to inspect defeats justifiable reliance in the face of active concealment.
reason.zh: 错误地暗示，面对主动隐瞒行为，未进行检验会否定合理信赖。

reason.en: Errs by ignoring that conduct (concealment) is legally equivalent to an affirmative assertion.
reason.zh: 错误地忽略了主动隐瞒行为在法律上等同于积极的事实陈述。

reason.en: Irrelevant defense because unconscionability requires unfair bargaining/terms, not simple fraud.
reason.zh: 无关的抗辩，因为显失公平要求显失公平的谈判或条款，而非单纯的欺诈。

reason.en: Identifies the dealer's state of mind required to establish a voidable contract due to fraud.
reason.zh: 确立了由于欺诈导致合同可撤销所需的车商主观心态。

reason.en: Properly identifies the physical actions treated as an untrue assertion of fact.
reason.zh: 正确识别出被法律视为不真实事实陈述的物理隐藏行为。

highlights.text: successfully concealing evidence of the accident

reason.en: This physical concealment acts as a misrepresentation of fact, making the contract voidable.
reason.zh: 这种物理上的隐瞒行为构成事实的虚假陈述，从而使合同可撤销。

highlights.text: buyer declined to have the car inspected by his own mechanic

reason.en: Triggers the issue of whether the buyer's reliance remained justifiable despite declining inspection.
reason.zh: 触发了关于买方在放弃检验的情况下其信赖是否仍然合理的争议点。

highlights.text: would rely on the dealer's certificate of assured quality

reason.en: Establishes the element of inducement and reliance on the dealer's misleading conduct.
reason.zh: 确立了诱导意图和对车商误导行为产生信赖的要件。

highlights.text: sues the dealer to rescind the transaction

reason.en: Sets the goal of the legal analysis to determine if the contract is voidable due to fraud.
reason.zh: 设定了法律分析的目标，即判断合同是否因欺诈而可撤销。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A professional race car driver decided to retire and sell his drag racing car. An amateur driver approached him about buying the car. The amateur driver explained that she needed a car that could complete a quarter-mile race in less than nine seconds, and the professional driver boasted that his car could do so in eight to nine seconds. Unbeknownst to the professional driver, there was a calibration error in his timing equipment, and the car had never completed a quarter-mile race in less than 10 seconds.
The two drivers settled on a price and signed a fully integrated, written contract. The amateur driver paid the sales price, took delivery of the car, and entered the next drag race. The car was unable to complete a quarter-mile race in less than 10 seconds, so the amateur driver contacted the professional driver and demanded her money back.
Is the professional driver obligated to return the amateur driver's money?

choices.A: No, because the professional driver's assertion was an unintentional misrepresentation.
choices.B: No, because the sales contract was memorialized in a fully integrated writing.
choices.C: Yes, because the professional driver's assertion was a fraudulent misrepresentation.
choices.D: Yes, because the professional driver's assertion was a material misrepresentation.

questions.explanation:
A misrepresentation is an untrue assertion of fact made during contract negotiations. This renders the contract voidable by the adversely affected party if:

  • the misrepresentation was fraudulent or material
  • the misrepresentation induced assent to the contract (presumed for material misrepresentations) and
  • the adversely affected party justifiably relied on the misrepresentation.

The justifiable-reliance element is essentially always met unless the misrepresentation was obviously false or known by the adversely affected party to be false.

Here, the professional driver falsely stated that his car could complete a quarter-mile race in eight to nine seconds. This misrepresentation was material and presumably induced the amateur driver to enter the contract since she had told the professional driver that she was looking for a car with that capability. The amateur driver's reliance on the misrepresentation was justifiable since it was not obviously false or known by her to be false. Therefore, the contract is voidable, and the professional driver is obligated to return the amateur driver's money.

(Choices A & C) A misrepresentation is fraudulent when it is made knowingly or recklessly, with intent to induce assent to the contract. Here, the professional driver's misrepresentation was nonfraudulent since he had timed his car and knew nothing about the calibration error in his timing equipment. But even an unintentional, nonfraudulent misrepresentation may be grounds to avoid a contract when, as here, the misrepresentation was material.

(Choice B) The parol evidence rule generally bars evidence of prior or contemporaneous agreements to modify or contradict the terms of an integrated writing. But such evidence is excepted from this rule and is admissible when it is offered to prove defenses to enforcement (eg, misrepresentation—as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A misrepresentation renders a contract voidable by the adversely affected party if (1) the misrepresentation was fraudulent or material, (2) it induced assent to the contract, and (3) the adversely affected party justifiably relied on it.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 159, 162, 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (defining material misrepresentation and explaining when it makes a contract voidable).
questions.zh-question:
一名职业赛车手决定退役并出售其直线加速赛车。一位业余车手找到他商谈购车事宜。该业余车手解释说，她需要一辆能在九秒内完成四分之一英里赛的赛车，而职业赛车手则声称他的车能在八到九秒内完成。职业赛车手并不知道，他的计时设备存在校准错误，该车从未在十秒内完成过四分之一英里赛。

两名车手谈妥了价格并签订了一份完全一体化的书面合同。业余车手支付了售价，接收了车辆，并参加了下一场直线加速赛。该车无法在十秒内完成四分之一英里赛，于是业余车手联系了职业赛车手，要求退还款项。

职业赛车手是否有义务退还业余车手的钱款？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为职业赛车手的陈述是无意的虚假陈述。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该销售合同已由一份完全一体化的书面文件正式记录。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为职业赛车手的陈述是欺诈性虚假陈述。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为职业赛车手的陈述是重大虚假陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖家明知或不知都不重要，只要对车辆性能作了重大失实陈述（material misrepresentation），买方就可以主张合同可撤销并追回价款。

三秒认题路径：

夸大车速 → 买方要性能 → 说错事实 → 诱使成交 → 可撤销

核心法律规则

先抓规则，再看这题怎么落地

虚假陈述（misrepresentation）是合同谈判中对事实作出的不真实陈述。若该陈述属于 欺诈性（fraudulent）或 重大（material），并诱使对方同意，且对方作出了正当依赖，受害方就可以撤销合同。

重大（material）的意思很直白：这句话会左右对方要不要签，所以考试上它不需要证明卖家故意撒谎。

正当依赖（justifiable reliance）的考场意思：只要对方没有明显看出是假话，也不知道是假话，通常就算依赖成立。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 159, 162, 164 — 这组规则直接锁定：重大失实陈述本身就能让合同可撤销，不必等到欺诈。

思维导图

卖家说“8到9秒跑完一英里四分之一”
先问：这话是真事实吗？
不是。实测从没低于 10 秒。先把“真实陈述”这道门关上。
再问：它只是普通吹牛，还是会影响成交？
会。买方明确说她要的是能达标的车，所以这是 material。
最后问：卖家一定要故意骗人吗？
不用。即使他不知道计时器校准出错，material misrepresentation 也足够。
结论：买方可撤销合同，选 Yes

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖家没有故意撒谎，所以买方不能退钱。

但考试真正问的是：这句话有没有骗到对方签约，而不是卖家主观上坏不坏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题还会骗你去想 fully integrated writing；但 parol evidence rule 允许为证明 misrepresentation 这类抗辩而引入合同外证据。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 买方明确要“九秒内”车辆，卖家却把实际 10秒以上 说成 8 到 9 秒，这正是可撤销的重大失实陈述。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 unintentional 当成免责点，忽略重大失实陈述不要求故意。

❌ 事实误判 | 书面效力偷换

✕ B: 盯着 fully integrated 就忘了，抗辩性欺诈/失实陈述可突破它。

❌ 法律适用 | 欺诈门槛抬高

✕ C: 把 fraudulent 当成唯一入口，漏掉了 material 也能撤销。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否有重大失实陈述，再看依赖，最后别被“非故意”和“整合书面”带偏。

考场速记

记住这句：虚假陈述可撤销；故意是加分项，不是必需项。看到买方明确说出用途，卖家又把关键性能说错，优先想 material misrepresentation。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A doctor was employed at a hospital when she applied for a personal loan from a bank. She accurately disclosed her income in the loan application. Before the bank had reached a decision regarding the loan application, the doctor was fired from the hospital. The doctor decided not to inform the bank of this fact because she feared that the bank would refuse to give her the loan.
A few days later, a bank representative called the doctor and informed her that her loan application was approved. The doctor accepted the terms of the loan and signed the loan agreement. Before disbursing the funds, the bank learned of the doctor's firing and refused to honor the loan agreement.
If the doctor sues the bank for breach of contract, will she be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the doctor's ability to repay the loan was a condition precedent to the disbursement of the funds.
choices.B: No, because the doctor's nondisclosure of her firing was a fraudulent misrepresentation.
choices.C: Yes, because the bank's reliance on the doctor's disclosure of her income in the loan application was unjustifiable.
choices.D: Yes, because the loan agreement was memorialized in a signed writing.

questions.explanation:
When disclosure is required to avoid misrepresentation
Previous assertion • Disclosure would prevent previous assertion from being a misrepresentation or fraudulent or material
Mistake about basic assumption • Disclosure would correct other party's mistake about basic assumption of contract
AND
• Failure to disclose would constitute lack of good faith & fair dealing
Fiduciary relationship • Other party is entitled to know fact because of confidential/fiduciary relationship
Mistake about writing • Disclosure would correct other party's mistake about contents or effect of writing that embodies agreement

A misrepresentation is an untrue assertion of fact that makes a contract voidable by the adversely affected party when all of the following elements are met:

  • The misrepresentation was fraudulent (ie, made knowingly or recklessly with the intent to induce the other party's assent to the contract) OR material (ie, likely to induce a reasonable person's assent).*
  • The misrepresentation induced assent to the contract.
  • The adversely affected party justifiably relied on the misrepresentation.

Nondisclosure of a known fact is treated as an untrue assertion if, among other things, the nondisclosing party knows that disclosure is necessary to prevent a previous assertion from being fraudulent.

Here, the doctor accurately disclosed her income in the loan application but was then fired. She knew that she needed to disclose this fact to the bank to prevent her previous disclosure from being fraudulent but failed to do so. Since the bank was unaware of her firing, it justifiably agreed to give her a loan. Therefore, the contract is voidable by the bank, and the doctor is unlikely to prevail in her breach-of-contract suit.

*A misrepresentation is also material if the maker knows that it will likely induce this particular party's assent—even if a reasonable person would not be induced.

(Choice A) A condition precedent is an explicit contract term requiring a future event to occur before a party becomes obligated to perform. But here, there is no indication that the bank's obligation to disburse the funds was explicitly conditioned on the doctor's ability to repay the loan.

(Choice C) Reliance is almost always justified unless the misrepresentation was obviously false or known by the adversely affected party to be false. Here, the doctor's disclosure was accurate (not obviously false) when it was made and the bank was unaware of her firing when it approved the loan, so the bank's reliance was justified.

(Choice D) The fact that the loan agreement was memorialized in a signed writing does not prevent it from being voidable on the basis of the doctor's fraudulent misrepresentation.

📌 Educational Objective

Nondisclosure of a known fact is treated as an untrue assertion of fact (ie, misrepresentation) if the nondisclosing party knows that disclosure is necessary to prevent a previous assertion from being fraudulent.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 161 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when nondisclosure is a misrepresentation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 164 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when misrepresentation makes a contract voidable).
questions.zh-question:
一名医生在医院工作时，向一家银行申请个人贷款。她在贷款申请中如实披露了其收入。在银行就其贷款申请做出决定之前，该医生被医院解雇。该医生决定不将此事告知银行，因为她担心银行会因此拒绝向她发放贷款。

几天后，一名银行代表致电该医生，通知她其贷款申请已获批准。该医生接受了贷款条款并签署了贷款协议。在发放资金前，银行得知了该医生被解雇一事，并拒绝履行贷款协议。

如果该医生以违约为由起诉银行，她是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为医生的还款能力是银行发放贷款的一项先决条件。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为医生未披露其被解雇一事构成了欺诈性虚假陈述。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为银行对医生在贷款申请中披露其收入的信赖是不正当的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为贷款协议已通过一份签署的书面文件予以确定。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to enforceability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：当一方在签约前知道自己先前的真实陈述已经不完整，却故意不补充时，这种 不披露（nondisclosure） 会不会被当成 虚假陈述（misrepresentation），从而让合同被对方撤销。

三秒认题路径：

先说真话 → 后来失真 → 明知不补 → 视为欺骗 → 合同可撤销

核心法律规则

在合同里，虚假陈述（misrepresentation） 不一定要嘴上说假话；如果你知道自己先前的陈述因为后来的事实变化已经会误导对方，而你还故意不补充，不披露（nondisclosure） 也会被当成错误陈述，考场意思：你不能靠“我没再说谎”来躲责。

只要这种不实信息是 fraudulent 或 material，并且对方据此同意、而且是 justifiably relied，合同就可能被对方撤销，考场意思：对方一旦被你带偏，后面签字也救不了你。

本题里最关键的是 Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 161：当你知道沉默会让先前真实陈述变成误导时，沉默本身就算 misrepresentation。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 161 与 § 164 一起锁定本题：银行有权因医生隐瞒失业事实而拒绝履行。

思维导图

先看：医生的“沉默”是不是只是没说话？
NO不是普通沉默，而是先前收入陈述已经会误导银行。
她是否知道：如果不补充“已被解雇”，前面的说法就会变假？
YES知道，所以 nondisclosure 变成 misrepresentation。
银行批准贷款后，能不能说自己仍可主张合同无效/可撤销？
YES可以，因为对方是被误导后才同意签约。
卡死点：不是看有没有写成书面，而是看这份书面是不是建立在欺骗上。
结论：银行胜，医生告违约大概率败诉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：医生已经把收入如实写在申请里，后来只是没更新新消息，所以不算骗。

但考试真正问的是：她明知失业会让之前的收入陈述继续误导银行，却故意不说，这就不是“安静”，而是“让对方继续被带偏”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 先如实报收入、后被解雇、却故意不补充，正好落入“为避免先前陈述变成虚假而应披露”的规则，所以银行可撤销合同。

❌ 事实误判 | 条件前提偷换

✕ A: 把贷款发放条件偷换成repay the loan 的前提。

❌ 法律适用 | 依赖标准错位

✕ C: 把银行的信赖说成不合理，但题目真正卡的是医生先前陈述已被后续事实弄成误导。

❌ 概念混淆 | 书面化免疫误判

✕ D: 以为signed writing 就能洗掉欺骗，但书面化不挡可撤销。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“先真后假”的事实链，再直接套 § 161 看沉默是否变成虚假陈述。

考场速记

记住一句：先前真话 + 后来失真 + 故意不补，就可能把沉默变成 misrepresentation。下次看到“先如实、后隐瞒”，优先想到银行或买方可以撤销，而不是先去想条件前提。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
A film star moved to the West Coast to further his acting career. He agreed to work for a motion picture studio for the next five years, leased a high-rise condominium for nine months, entered an agreement to purchase an exotic sports car for $250,000, and agreed to transfer ownership of his beach house to his girlfriend if she married him.
Which of these transactions is most likely to be enforceable without a signed writing?

choices.A: The employment agreement with the motion picture studio.
choices.B: The lease agreement with the luxury condominium corporation.
choices.C: The purchase agreement for the sports car.
choices.D: The agreement to transfer the beach house to the girlfriend.

questions.explanation:
The statute of frauds requires the following contracts to be evidenced by a writing that contains all essential terms and is signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought (MY LEGS):

  • Marriage – a contract made in consideration of marriage
  • Year – a contract that cannot be completed within one year
  • Land – a contract for the sale or transfer of an interest in real property
  • Executor – a contract to pay an estate's debt out of the executor's personal funds
  • Goods – a contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more
  • Suretyship – a contract to answer for the debt or duty of another

Therefore, in this scenario, the following transactions must be evidenced by a signed writing to be enforceable:

  • • The five-year employment agreement with the motion picture studio because it cannot be completed in less than one year (Choice A)
  • • The purchase agreement for the sports car (a good) because the $250,000 sales price exceeds $500 (Choice C)
  • • The agreement to transfer ownership of the beach house to the girlfriend because it (1) involves an interest in real property and (2) was made in consideration of her marriage to the film star (Choice D)

However, the nine-month lease agreement with the luxury condominium corporation does not fall under the statute of frauds—even though it involves an interest in real property. The reason is that leases and easements for less than one year are usually excluded from the statute.* Therefore, this transaction is most likely to be enforceable without a signed writing.

*Licenses and assignments of mortgages are also excluded from the statute of frauds.

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts that fall under the statute of frauds (MY LEGS) must be contained in a signed writing to be enforceable. Although this generally includes contracts involving an interest in real property, leases and easements for less than one year do not fall under the statute.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 127 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (interests in land subject to the statute of frauds).
questions.zh-question:
一位电影明星为了发展其演艺事业，搬到了西海岸。他同意为一家电影制片厂工作五年，租用了一套高层公寓九个月，签订了一份以25万美元购买一辆珍奇跑车的协议，并同意如果女友与他结婚，就将海滨别墅的所有权转让给她。

在这些交易中，哪一项最有可能在没有书面签署的情况下具有强制执行力？

zh-choices.A: 与电影制片厂签订的雇佣协议。
zh-choices.B: 与豪华公寓公司签订的租赁协议。
zh-choices.C: 跑车的购买协议。
zh-choices.D: 将海滨别墅转让给女友的协议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：哪些合同掉进 防止欺诈法（Statute of Frauds），以及哪一种 一年以下的房屋租赁（lease under one year） 反而不用签字写明也能执行。

三秒认题路径：

先找 SOF → 再看 MY LEGS → 排除<1年租赁 → 选可口头执行

核心法律规则

防止欺诈法（Statute of Frauds）要求某些合同必须有书面证据，而且要由被请求履行的一方签字。考试里先记住 MY LEGS：婚姻、一年规则（year）、土地、遗嘱执行人、商品、保证。

本题里，五年雇佣合同（year）、25万美元汽车买卖（goods）、为结婚而转让海边房屋（marriage/land） 都要书面；只有 九个月公寓租约（lease） 因为少于一年，通常被排除在外，所以最可能无需签字也能强制执行。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 127 说明土地利益通常进 SOF，但少于一年的租赁通常不进，正好锁定本题结论。

思维导图

先问：这笔交易是不是 防止欺诈法（Statute of Frauds） 要求书面？
是 MY LEGS 里任一项命中，就要书面 + 签字
A 五年雇佣 → 一年不能完成（year） → 要书面
C 汽车买卖 → 商品（goods） 且远超 $500 → 要书面
D 海边房屋转让 → 土地（land） + 婚姻对价（marriage） → 要书面
否
九个月公寓租约 → lease under one year → 通常不进 SOF
结论 这条路最可能 无需签字也能执行 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这个公寓租约也碰到 土地利益（interest in real property），所以应该要书面。

但考试真正问的是：它是不是 少于一年（less than one year） 的租赁。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里的重点不是“和土地有关就一定进 SOF”，而是看有没有落进少于一年租赁这个排除项。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 nine-month lease 是少于一年的租约，通常不进 Statute of Frauds，所以不需要 signed writing 也最可能可执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 年度规则误判

✕ A: 把 five years 忘成可口头履行了。

❌ 法律适用 | 商品门槛误判

✕ C: 看到 $500 以上却没想到商品买卖必须书面。

❌ 事实误判 | 婚姻对价偷换

✕ D: 把 married him 当成无关赠与，漏掉婚姻对价和土地转让双重触发。

这题建议用什么方法？

先用 MY LEGS 快速扫一遍，再优先抓 lease under one year 这个排除项。

考场速记

记忆口诀：MY LEGS 先扫一遍；遇到租约先问“有没有 少于一年”，有就别急着套 SOF。土地相关不等于一定要书面，一年以下租赁（lease under one year） 是经典例外。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A woman owned a large ranch, which she orally offered to sell to her stable manager for $250,000. The stable manager eagerly accepted her offer, and the woman wrote and gave him an unsigned note that read, "I agree to sell you my ranch for $250,000."
The stable manager gave the woman a small down payment to seal the deal and then took possession of the ranch with the woman's permission. Shortly thereafter, the stable manager received a letter from the woman stating that another buyer had offered to buy the ranch for $425,000 and that she would not sell it to the stable manager unless he buys it for that price.
If the stable manager sues the woman for specific performance, which of the following concepts would best support his claim?

choices.A: Anticipatory breach.
choices.B: Good faith and fair dealing.
choices.C: Part performance.
choices.D: Quantum meruit.

questions.explanation:
The statute of frauds applies to contracts for the sale of land (eg, the ranch). It requires that the contract (1) be in writing, (2) be signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought, and (3) contain all essential terms. Therefore, the woman and stable manager's oral agreement and the woman's unsigned note each violated this statute.

However, a contract for the sale of land that violates this statute may still be enforceable if the part-performance exception applies. This requires proof that the buyer has done at least two of the following:

  • • Taken possession of the property (as the stable manager did here)
  • • Made substantial improvements to the property (not seen here)
  • • Paid some or all of the purchase price (here, the stable manager made a small down payment)

The buyer can then bring an action in equity for specific performance. However, part performance will not support an ordinary action at law for money damages.

(Choice A) Anticipatory breach* occurs when one party communicates to the other party that it will not perform under the contract. The other party can treat this as a breach and sue immediately or demand performance. Here, although the woman told the stable manager that she would not sell him the ranch for the agreed-upon price, this would not overcome the statute of frauds.

*This is also called anticipatory repudiation.

(Choice B) The duty of good faith and fair dealing implied in every contract requires that neither party interfere with the other party's performance of the contract or right to receive the benefits thereof. But the stable manager cannot assert a breach of this duty without first proving that an enforceable contract exists.

(Choice D) Quantum meruit entitles a party who has conferred a benefit on another in a quasi-contractual relationship to damages for the reasonable value of the benefit, but not specific performance.

📌 Educational Objective

A contract involving land that violates the statute of frauds is enforceable on part-performance grounds if the buyer has done at least two of the following: taken possession of the property, substantially improved it, and/or paid any portion of the purchase price.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 129 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (action in reliance; specific performance).

一名女士拥有一座大牧场，她口头要约以25万美元的价格将其出售给她的马厩经理。马厩经理欣然接受了她的要约，该女士写了一张未签署的便条交给他，内容是：“我同意以25万美元的价格将我的牧场卖给你。”

为了达成交易，马厩经理向该女士支付了一小笔首付款，然后在该女士的许可下占有了该牧场。此后不久，马厩经理收到了该女士的一封信，信中称另一位买家已要约以42.5万美元的价格购买该牧场，除非马厩经理以该价格购买，否则她不会将牧场出售给他。

如果马厩经理就特定履行起诉该女士，以下哪个概念最能支持他的主张？

zh-choices.A: 预期违约。
zh-choices.B: 诚信与公平交易原则。
zh-choices.C: 部分履行。
zh-choices.D: Quantum meruit.

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to enforceability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：土地买卖合同触犯 书面形式要求（statute of frauds） 后，买方能不能靠 部分履行（part performance） 直接拿到 衡平法上的强制履行（specific performance）。

三秒认题路径：

土地买卖 → 口头合同 → 已进场+已付款 → 部分履行 → 可强制履行

核心法律规则

土地买卖合同（contract for the sale of land）一般必须写成书面，并由被要求履行的一方签字；这里女人只给了 unsigned note，所以先卡在 statute of frauds。

但如果买方做了至少两件事，法院会更愿意相信这不是空口说白话：占有（possession）、重大改良（substantial improvements）、支付价款（payment of purchase price）。这题里稳定经理已经 拿到土地并付了定金，所以能走 part performance 去争取 specific performance。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 129 — 买方在土地合同上做了足够的依赖行为时，可以用部分履行突破书面形式要求，去要衡平救济。

思维导图

卖方口头承诺 土地合同先天要写书面
→
无签字书面 statute of frauds 先被击中
→
买方占有 + 付定金 两项依赖行为已出现
→
卡死点：不是钱赔不赔，而是能不能拿到房产 可走 part performance 衡平法支持 specific performance

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖方后来明确说“我不卖了”，所以应该抓 anticipatory breach（预期违约）。

但考试真正问的是：口头土地合同在 statute of frauds 下能不能先活下来；这里要先看 part performance，不是先追违约名号。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里买方已经占有牧场并付了小额定金，正好凑到部分履行的核心触发点，所以可支持 specific performance。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 anticipatory breach 当成能绕开书面要求的钥匙了。

❌ 法律适用 | 先后顺序错位

✕ B: 先有可执行合同才谈 good faith，这里还卡在形式瑕疵。

❌ 事实误判 | 救济类型偷换

✕ D: quantum meruit 只能算合理价款，不是拿房子的路。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否落入书面形式要求，再数买方有没有做出足够的依赖行为。

考场速记

记住这句：土地合同先看书面，救济再看部分履行；买方只要常见的两项依赖动作到位，就可以往 specific performance 方向想。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An elderly woman underwent major surgery and spent two weeks in the hospital. The woman continued to take powerful pain medication for several weeks after she returned home. During her recovery, she offered to sell her car for $450 to her neighbor, who owned a house-cleaning service. The neighbor said, "That's great! I need a car to transport all the people who work for me to their job sites."
In fact, the woman's car was worth $3,000, and the neighbor knew this. He was also aware that the woman had undergone surgery and noted that she seemed "out of it" because of the medication she was taking.
Several days later, the woman's son found out about the deal and contacted the neighbor, telling him that the woman would sell him the car, but for $3,450. The next day, when the neighbor tendered $450 and demanded that the woman give him the car, she refused.
If the neighbor sues the woman for breach of contract, will he be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the contract was voidable due to the woman's apparent incapacity.
choices.B: No, because the woman put nothing in writing.
choices.C: Yes, because the neighbor's reliance on the otherwise voidable contract made it enforceable.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman's offer and the neighbor's acceptance created an enforceable contract.

questions.explanation:
Incapacity to form contract
Infancy
  • Person under 18 enters contract
  • Voidable if disaffirmed by minor before or soon after turning 18
  • Minor must return any still-existing benefit received under contract
Mental illness
  • Void if incapacitated party has been adjudicated incompetent
  • Voidable if:
    • mental capacity so deficient that party cannot reasonably understand (or act in relation to) nature or consequences of contract AND other party had reason to know or
    • disaffirmed by incapacitated party when lucid or by legal representative
Intoxication
  • Party too intoxicated to reasonably understand (or act in relation to) nature or consequences of contract AND other party had reason to know
  • Voidable if promptly disaffirmed by intoxicated party upon becoming sober
  • Intoxicated party must offer to return any consideration received & may be liable for fair value of goods or services provided

A valid contract is generally formed when a mutual agreement is supported by adequate consideration—eg, when the woman offered to sell her car and the neighbor accepted. That contract is enforceable unless the breaching party establishes a defense (Choice D). Incapacity due to intoxication is a defense when:

  • an intoxicated party could not reasonably understand or act in relation to the nature or consequences of the contract (eg, selling a car worth $3,000 for only $450) and
  • the other party had reason to know of the intoxication (eg, noticing that the intoxicated party was "out of it" when the contract was formed).

This renders a contract voidable, so it can be set aside if the intoxicated party acts promptly (ie, within a reasonable time) to disaffirm it upon becoming sober. And here, the woman likely was still under medication when she disaffirmed the contract by refusing to give the neighbor the car, so the neighbor is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice B) A contract need only be in writing and signed by the party to be charged if it falls within the statute of frauds. This rule applies to contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more, but it does not apply to this contract to sell the car for only $450.

(Choice C) Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, a party can enforce a promise on which it relied when no valid contract was formed. But the doctrine only allows recovery if the party's reliance was reasonable and caused substantial detriment—neither of which is seen here.

📌 Educational Objective

Incapacity due to intoxication renders a contract voidable if the intoxicated party could not reasonably understand the nature or consequences of the contract AND the other party had reason to know of the intoxication. The contract can then be set aside if the intoxicated party promptly disaffirms it upon becoming sober.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 12–16 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (incapacity to contract).
questions.zh-question:
一位老妇人接受了一次大手术，并在医院住了两周。回家后，这位妇人继续服用了几周的强效止痛药。在康复期间，她向她拥有一家房屋清洁公司的邻居提出以450美元的价格出售她的汽车。邻居说：“太好了！我需要一辆车来运送为我工作的所有人去他们的工作地点。”

事实上，这位妇人的汽车价值3000美元，邻居也知道这一点。他还知道这位妇人做过手术，并注意到由于她正在服用的药物，她看起来“精神恍惚”。

几天后，这位妇人的儿子发现了这笔交易，并联系了邻居，告诉他妇人愿意卖车给他，但价格是3450美元。第二天，当邻居支付了450美元并要求妇人把车给他时，她拒绝了。

如果邻居以违约为由起诉这位妇人，他是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为由于该妇人明显的行为能力欠缺，该合同是可撤销的。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该妇人没有订立任何书面协议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为邻居对本可撤销的合同的信赖使其变得可强制执行。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该妇人的要约和邻居的承诺创造了一份可强制执行的合同。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：醉酒或药物影响下的 合同缔约能力（capacity to contract） 是否足以让合同变成可撤销合同，所以邻居不能只盯着“已经同意了”这一步。

三秒认题路径：

看“out of it” → 看知情 → 看可撤销 → 看及时撤销 → 看能否强制履行

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

合同缔约能力（capacity）不够时，合同通常不是自动无效，而是可撤销（voidable）。如果一方因酒精、药物或其他原因，could not reasonably understand 合同性质或后果，而且对方知道或应知（reason to know），这份合同就能被弱势方撤销。

考试上最关键的是：对方后来就算拿着“我已经接受了”来起诉，也会卡在这个防御事由上；只要弱势方在恢复清醒后及时拒绝履行，邻居就很难赢。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 12–16 — 锁定“能力不足 + 对方知情 → 合同可撤销”的考试结论。

思维导图

先问：这份合同能不能因为能力问题被撤销？
第1步当事人是否因 药物影响（intoxication / medication） 不能合理理解交易？
本题老妇人术后还在吃强效止痛药，且把 $3,000 的车卖 $450，明显像“脑子不清楚”。
第2步对方是否知道或应知？
本题邻居看出她 “out of it”，这就补上了知情要件。
第3步一旦满足，合同变成 voidable，不是邻居想当然地“当然有效”
第4步她恢复后及时拒绝交车 = disaffirm，邻居想靠强制履行会失败。
答案选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她开口报价、对方也说接受了，offer and acceptance 都齐了，所以合同一定能执行。

但考试真正问的是：她当时有没有能力做出有效承诺；如果她被药物弄得“脑子不清楚”，合同就先天带着可撤销问题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里 术后长期服用强效止痛药，又把 $3,000 的车卖 $450，邻居还看出她“out of it”，正好满足可撤销的能力缺陷与知情要件。

❌ 事实误判 | 书面要件偷换

✕ B: 把 writing 硬套进来，但这不是法条书面要件题。

❌ 法律适用 | 依赖救济误判

✕ C: 想用 promissory estoppel 把本来可撤销的合同硬变成可执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 形式成立误认

✕ D: 只看到 acceptance，却漏了能力缺陷这个防御事由。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看当事人有没有能力，再看对方是否知情，最后才判断合同能不能被及时撤销。

考场速记

记住：能力不足 + 对方知情 = 可撤销。一旦弱势方恢复后及时拒绝履行，对方通常不能靠“我已接受”把合同硬推成有效。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A cattle rancher operates a large ranch with many employees. State law requires all employees within the state to pay a state income tax, and all employers are required to accurately report their employees' incomes. Enforcement of the state law is a civil matter. There are no criminal penalties for failure to pay or failure to accurately report.
The rancher entered a written employment contract with a veterinarian, who agreed to manage the health of the rancher's cattle for six months. Both parties knew about the state income tax, and the veterinarian wanted to avoid paying it. The rancher therefore agreed to compensate the veterinarian by paying the veterinarian's monthly mortgage directly to the bank without reporting the payments to the state. The rancher paid the veterinarian's mortgage for the first three months of the contract and then stopped making payments even though the veterinarian continued to work.
If the veterinarian sues the rancher, what will he likely recover?

choices.A: Expectation damages, because the rancher breached the contract and it did not involve any criminal conduct.
choices.B: Restitution damages, because the rancher withdrew from the agreement by failing to make additional mortgage payments.
choices.C: Restitution damages, because the veterinarian was less culpable than the rancher.
choices.D: Nothing, because the contract had an illegal purpose.

questions.explanation:
Recovery for breach of illegal contract

Purpose, formation, or performance
of contract against law
No remedy for breach
Exceptions
(alternative theories of recovery)
Expectation damages
  • Justifiably ignorant of illegality
  • Substantial performance & no illegal purpose
  • Legal separable from illegal parts or
  • Illegality for violating revenue-raising licensing requirement
Recover full value of
lost performance
OR
Restitution damages
  • Justifiably ignorant of illegality
  • Less culpable than other party or
  • Withdrew from contract & did not engage in serious misconduct
Recover reasonable value
of benefit conferred

An illegal contract arises when one or both parties' purpose, formation, or performance is against the law—such as the rancher's agreement not to report the veterinarian's income as required by state law. Such contracts generally are void and there is no remedy for breach. However, an illegal contract is enforceable for the full amount of the nonbreaching party's expectation damages if:

  • the nonbreaching party was justifiably ignorant of the facts that made the contract illegal*
  • the nonbreaching party substantially performed and lacked an illegal purpose
  • the contract can be easily separated into legal and illegal parts or
  • the contract is illegal due to a violation of a licensing requirement designed only to raise revenue.

None of these exceptions apply here. The veterinarian knew about the state income tax and purposely contracted to evade it. The agreed method of compensation is entirely illegal and cannot be separated from any legal part. Additionally, the illegality does not stem from a licensing violation. As a result, the veterinarian cannot recover expectation damages (Choice A).

However, restitution damages may be an alternative form of recovery. A party to an illegal contract can recover such damages if that party conferred a benefit on the other party and:

  • was justifiably ignorant of the facts that made the contract illegal*
  • was less culpable than the other party or
  • withdrew before the contract's illegal purpose was achieved and did not engage in serious misconduct.

Here, both parties knew about the law, so they were equally culpable in agreeing to violate it (Choice C). And only after the contract's illegal purpose was achieved through the first few payments did the rancher (not the veterinarian) withdraw by failing to make additional payments (Choice B). Therefore, the veterinarian also cannot recover restitution damages.

*However, recovery on this basis will be barred if the other party also was justifiably ignorant.

📌 Educational Objective

An illegal contract generally is void and there is no remedy for a breach. However, in limited situations, a party to an illegal contract can recover either expectation damages (eg, if the party was justifiably ignorant of the illegality) OR restitution damages (eg, if the party was less culpable than the other party).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 178 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining when promises are unenforceable on public-policy grounds).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 197–199 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (availability of restitution).
questions.zh-question:
一个牧场主经营着一个拥有众多雇员的大型牧场。州法律要求州内所有雇员缴纳州所得税，并要求所有雇主准确申报其雇员的收入。该州法律的执行属于民事事宜。未缴税或未准确申报并无刑事处罚。

该牧场主与一名兽医签订了书面雇佣合同，兽医同意在六个月内管理牧场牛群的健康。双方都知道州所得税的存在，且兽医想逃避缴纳该税款。因此，牧场主同意通过直接向银行支付兽医的月度按揭贷款来补偿兽医，而不向州政府申报这些款项。牧场主在合同的前三个月支付了兽医的按揭贷款，但随后尽管兽医继续工作，牧场主却停止了支付。

如果兽医起诉牧场主，他可能获得什么赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 预期损害赔偿金，因为牧场主违反了合同，且合同不涉及任何犯罪行为。
zh-choices.B: 返还性损害赔偿金，因为牧场主未能支付后续的按揭贷款，从而退出了协议。
zh-choices.C: 返还性损害赔偿金，因为兽医的过错程度低于牧场主。
zh-choices.D: 无法获得任何赔偿，因为该合同具有非法目的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to Enforcement

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非法合同（illegal contract）通常不能请求违约救济，且本题里也没有任何可用的期待利益或返还利益例外。

三秒认题路径：

合同行为违法 → 目的就是逃税 → 无救济 → 例外都不成 → 选 D

核心法律规则

如果合同的目的（purpose）、成立（formation）或履行（performance）本身违法，这份合同通常无效（void），也就没有违约救济。

题目里双方明知要用合同安排去逃税（evade tax），而且付款方式本身就是违法安排，所以不能靠 expectation damages 追“本来应得的利润”。

也不能靠 restitution damages 绕回来，因为这里不是无辜一方；双方都知道违法目的，且兽医也不是在违法目的未完成前自行退出的一方。

核心判例： 本题按非法合同的普通规则处理：知道违法目的还一起做，法院通常不会帮你把合同救活。

思维导图

这份合同是不是把“违法”写进了目的或履行方式？
是：合同核心就是逃税（tax evasion），先判定无违约救济。
再问例外：能不能拿 expectation damages？
只有在“对违法不知情 / 只碰到合法部分 / 可切割 / 低风险许可费”这类例外里才可能拿到；本题都没有。
再问返还：能不能拿 restitution damages？
不能。双方都知情，兽医不是更无辜的一方，也不是先撤出违法计划的人。
结论：既拿不到期待利益，也拿不到返还利益 → D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然牧场主先付了三个月，兽医至少能拿回已经提供服务的那部分。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是一份以违法目的为核心的合同；如果是，先别急着算钱，先看法院愿不愿意帮你开救济口子。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

本题里双方都知道要用隐瞒工资的方式逃税，所以“我已经干活了”不会自动变成可执行的债权。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 按月代付房贷 本身就是为逃避州所得税的违法对价安排，所以合同无效，兽医不能拿任何违约救济。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“没犯罪”当成“可执行”，误以为民事违法合同也能照赔。

❌ 事实误判 | 退出时点偷换

✕ B: 把 withdrew 说成兽医撤出，但真正停付的人是牧场主。

❌ 法律适用 | 责任轻重误判

✕ C: 以为“谁更坏谁输”，但本题双方都知情，没法靠更低 culpability 翻盘。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓违法目的，再按“期待利益 / 返还利益”两道例外逐个排除。

考场速记

记忆口诀：违法合同先判无效，再看例外有没有“无辜、可切割、先退出”。

这题最实用的速记是：知道违法还一起做，通常就别指望法院帮你算违约金。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A landowner, having suffered severe losses on bad investments, was money-poor but land-rich by inheritance, owning several thousand acres of unencumbered timberland. He had a large family, and his fixed personal expenses were high. Pressed for cash, he advertised a proposed sale of standing timber on a choice 2,000-acre tract. The only response was an offer by a logger who owned a large, integrated construction enterprise, after inspection of the advertised tract.
The logger offered to buy, sever, and remove the standing timber from the advertised tract at a cash price 70% lower than the regionally prevailing price for comparable timber rights. The landholder, by then in desperate financial straits and knowing little about timber values, signed and delivered to the logger a letter accepting the offer.
If, before the logger commences performance, the landholder's investment fortunes suddenly improve and he wishes to get out of the timber deal with the logger, which of the following legal concepts affords his best prospect of effective cancellation?

choices.A: Bad faith.
choices.B: Duress.
choices.C: Equitable estoppel.
choices.D: Unconscionability.

questions.explanation:
The defense of unconscionability is available when a contract's bargaining process and/or the contract terms were so unfair to one party that no reasonable person would have agreed to it. When this occurs, the court can modify or cancel (ie, refuse to enforce) the contract. Factors used to determine whether a contract is unconscionable include:

  • sophistication and knowledge of each party (eg, the parties' unequal knowledge of the timber industry)
  • disparity between the parties' bargaining power (eg, the landowner is money-poor and the logger is the only potential buyer)
  • disparity between the value of consideration exchanged by the parties (eg, the sale of timber rights on choice land for a price that is significantly lower than the prevailing rate) and
  • one-sidedness of contract terms (eg, the contract terms overwhelmingly favor the logger).

Therefore, unconscionability provides the landowner his best prospect of effective cancellation of the contract.

(Choice A) Good faith and fair dealing demand only actual honesty; here, there is no indication that the logger failed to meet this standard. Therefore, bad faith is not the landowner's best argument.

(Choice B) Duress serves as a defense to contract enforceability only if a contracting party's assent was induced by an improper threat—which did not occur here.

(Choice C) Equitable estoppel is a doctrine that prevents one party from changing its position after the other party has detrimentally relied on a misrepresentation of fact made by the first party. Here, however, the logger did not make a misrepresentation of fact to the landowner, so this doctrine does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

A party may assert the defense of unconscionability if the bargaining process and/or terms of the contract were so unfair to that party when the contract was made that no reasonable person would have agreed to it.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 208 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (unconscionable contract or contract term).
questions.zh-question:
一位土地所有者，因不良投资遭受严重损失，继承了数千英亩无产权负担的林地，因而土地富裕但现金贫乏。他家庭人口众多，个人固定开支高昂。在现金的压力下，他刊登广告，提议出售一块2000英亩优选地块上的立木。唯一的响应来自一位拥有大型综合建筑企业的伐木工，他在视察了广告中的地块后发出了要约。

伐木工要约以比该地区可比木材权通行价格低70%的现金价格，购买、砍伐并移走广告地块上的立木。土地所有者当时正处于绝望的财务困境中，且对木材价值知之甚少，他签署并向伐木工交付了一封信函，接受了该要约。

如果在伐木工开始履行合同之前，土地所有者的投资运势突然好转，并希望退出与伐木工的木材交易，那么以下哪个法律概念为他有效取消合同提供了最佳前景？

zh-choices.A: 恶意。
zh-choices.B: 胁迫。
zh-choices.C: 衡平法上的禁止反言。
zh-choices.D: 不合情理。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to Enforcement

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：合同已经签了，但条款和议价过程太不公平时，能不能用 显失公平（unconscionability） 直接把交易掀翻。

三秒认题路径：

低价砍树 → 买方更强 → 条款失衡 → 当事人不公 → 显失公平（unconscionability）

核心法律规则

显失公平（unconscionability）考场意思：签约当时如果议价过程或合同条款对一方 so unfair，以至于理性人不会签，法院可以拒绝执行，甚至修改或撤销合同。

判断时重点看四个信号：双方是否 知识与经验（sophistication and knowledge） 差很多、议价力量（bargaining power） 是否严重失衡、交换对价是否差得离谱、条款是否明显一边倒。

这题里，地主 缺钱但懂得少（money-poor, knowledge-poor），买方是唯一买家，还用 比地区市价低70% 的价格拿下木材权，最像的就是 显失公平（unconscionability）。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 208 - 这条规则就是用来锁定“签约时太不公平，所以法院可以不执行”。

思维导图

先看：这题是不是在找“能不能取消合同”的防御？
是进入无效抗辩筛选。
有没有 不当威胁（improper threat） 逼他签？
没有威胁 → 胁迫（duress） 直接出局。
有没有一方先作出 事实误导（misrepresentation of fact），对方再据此改变立场？
没有误导 → 衡平禁止反言（equitable estoppel） 不进场。
议价过程 + 价格 + 经验 + 力量，是否一起指向“太不公平”？
签约时就失衡 → 选 显失公平（unconscionability）。
结果
D. Unconscionability

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然地主后来想毁约，就该去找 bad faith、duress，或者说对方太占便宜所以能翻案。

但考试真正问的是：签约那一刻有没有一种“法院可以不执行”的防御，重点看交易本身是否过于失衡，而不是事后谁反悔、谁更倒霉。

bad faith 只管诚实与否；duress 需要不当威胁；equitable estoppel 需要对方先做事实误导并引人信赖，这三条都没打中。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里的 70% 低于市价、唯一买家、地主又懂得少，正好凑出签约时的严重失衡，所以最有力的取消理由是 显失公平（unconscionability）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 你把 good faith 当成“太不公平就能毁约”，但这里没说对方撒谎或不诚实。

❌ 法律适用 | 威胁要件误判

✕ B: 你想找 improper threat，可题干只有低价交易，没有逼迫签字的威胁。

❌ 事实误判 | 误导事实偷换

✕ C: 你硬塞 misrepresentation，但买方只是出价，并没有先说假事实让地主去信。

这题建议用什么方法？

先排除“威胁”和“误导”，再看签约当时是否已经不公平到法院不愿执行。

考场速记

记住一句：显失公平（unconscionability） 盯的是“签约时是否太黑”，不是“事后谁后悔”。

速记法：Unfair process + unfair terms = no enforcement；只要看到“低价 + 弱势一方 + 唯一买家 + 条款偏一边”，先想它。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
An aircraft broker sought to purchase on behalf of its client a private jet from a fleet owned by a corporation. In a telephone conversation between the broker and the corporation's finance manager, the broker offered $9 million for the jet. The manager agreed on the condition that the broker give the corporation a $250,000 deposit toward the jet's purchase price and a copy of the broker's agreement with the client. The broker complied with the manager's request.
Subsequently, the broker and the corporation exchanged written drafts of a contract memorializing their agreement. None of the drafts were signed by the parties. Two months later, the corporation notified the broker that the jet was not for sale and disputed the existence of an enforceable contract.
Is there an enforceable contract between the broker and the corporation?

choices.A: No, because partial payment of the jet's purchase price did not take the contract out of the statute of frauds.
choices.B: No, because the broker never signed a writing evidencing a contract with the corporation.
choices.C: Yes, because the agreement was memorialized in the written drafts of the contract exchanged by the parties.
choices.D: Yes, because the broker paid $250,000 for the jet and the corporation accepted that payment.

questions.explanation:
UCC statute of frauds exceptions

The UCC statute of frauds applies to contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more (eg, private jet sold for $9 million). These contracts generally must be in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought to be enforceable. However, one exception applies when some amount of payment was made and accepted.* The effect of a partial payment turns on whether the contract is for:

  • separable goods – in which case, the contract is enforceable up to the quantity of goods paid for in full or
  • an indivisible good – in which case, the entire contract is enforceable.

Here, the broker–corporation contract violated the statute of frauds because none of the written drafts exchanged by the parties were signed (Choice C). However, the broker paid $250,000 (partial payment) toward the jet (indivisible good) and the corporation presumably accepted that payment. Therefore, the contract is excepted from the statute of frauds and is enforceable in its entirety (Choice A).

*The exception also applies when some amount of goods have been received and accepted.

(Choice B) The fact that the broker never signed a writing evidencing a contract with the corporation is irrelevant. That is because the corporation is the party against whom enforcement is sought and the one whose signature was therefore needed to satisfy the statute of frauds.

📌 Educational Objective

A contract is excepted from the UCC statute of frauds when some amount of payment was made and accepted. A partial payment for separable goods renders the contract enforceable only up to the quantity paid for in full, while a partial payment for an indivisible good renders the entire contract enforceable.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-201 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (statute of frauds formal requirements).
questions.zh-question:
一家飞机经纪商代表其客户，寻求从一家公司拥有的机队中购买一架私人飞机。在经纪商与该公司财务经理的电话交谈中，经纪商要约以900万美元购买该飞机。经理同意了，条件是经纪商向公司支付25万美元的定金作为飞机购买价款的一部分，并提供一份经纪商与其客户之间的协议副本。经纪商遵守了经理的要求。

随后，经纪商和公司交换了书面合同草案以记录他们的协议。双方均未签署任何草案。两个月后，该公司通知经纪商，该飞机不再出售，并对是否存在可强制执行的合同提出异议。

经纪商与公司之间是否存在可强制执行的合同？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为部分支付飞机购买价款并未使合同免于欺诈法的规定。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为经纪商从未签署任何证明与公司存在合同的书面文件。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为协议已记录在双方交换的合同书面草案中。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为经纪商为该飞机支付了25万美元，且公司接受了该笔付款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC《statute of frauds》下，部分付款（partial payment）加上卖方收下这笔钱，能不能把这份不可分割货物（indivisible good）买卖合同救活。

三秒认题路径：

货物超额 → 书面缺签 → 付款已收 → 看例外 → 整份可执行

核心法律规则

UCC 下，金额达到 $500 以上的货物买卖合同（sale of goods）一般要有书面并由被起诉的一方签名，考场意思：没有签字通常就卡在《statute of frauds》。

但如果一方已经付款、另一方也收了这笔钱，就触发部分付款例外（partial payment exception），考场意思：这份合同不再因为“没写纸面”而自动死掉。

关键还要看货物是可分割（separable goods）还是不可分割（indivisible good）：可分割时只保到已付清的数量；不可分割时，整份合同都能被执行。

核心判例： 这里直接按 UCC § 2-201 的规则走，不需要额外判例。真正锁定结论的是“已付款且已被接受”这一例外。

思维导图

先看：这是不是货物买卖且金额 ≥ $500？
是 进入 UCC《statute of frauds》：通常要书面签名。
但本题 双方只交换了未签名草稿，书面要求本来没过。
再问 有没有 部分付款（partial payment） 且对方已收下？
有 对于 不可分割货物（indivisible good），整份合同可执行。
本题落点 250,000 美元定金已付且已收，故答案是 D。
不是 直接回到普通合同规则，不走这题。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然没有签字，那就一定不能执行，尤其看到 signed writing 会很容易选“不”。

但考试真正问的是：部分付款并被接受 这个例外有没有把合同救回来，而不是死盯着“有没有签名”这一层。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的钱有没有真的离开手里」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 $250,000 已付且已被公司接受，而飞机是不可分割货物（indivisible good），所以这个 partial payment 例外把整份合同救活了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 误以为partial payment 完全没用，忽略了已收款的例外效力。

❌ 事实误判 | 签字对象错认

✕ B: 把签字责任丢给 broker，但被追责的一方是 corporation，签名缺口不在这里。

❌ 法律适用 | 书面草稿误当正式签署

✕ C: 把未签名草稿当成memorialized 的正式书面，其实还差签字这一步。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看《statute of frauds》门槛，再专找“付款已付且已收”的例外，不要被未签字草稿带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：货物大额买卖先看书面，已付款并被接受就看例外；若是不可分割货物，通常能直接把整份合同救回来。
