questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds
questions.question:
A commercial baker and an ingredient supplier orally agreed that the baker would purchase 1,000 pounds of flour from the supplier for a price between 50 and 75 cents per pound. The parties agreed that they would determine the final price upon delivery. The supplier promised to deliver the flour in two weeks.
Later that day, the baker sent the supplier a signed note reminding the supplier about the terms of their agreement, including the quantity of flour. The supplier received the note, read it, and took no further action. When the supplier failed to deliver the flour, the baker sued the supplier for breach of contract.
Can the baker enforce the contract against the supplier?

choices.A: No, because the parties did not agree to a definitive price term.
choices.B: No, because the supplier did not sign the note.
choices.C: Yes, because the baker sent the supplier a signed confirmation.
choices.D: Yes, because the parties' oral agreement is enforceable.

questions.explanation:
Statute of frauds requirements
Writing Physical or electronic document(s) containing reasonable basis to believe contract was formed (eg, receipt, check, emails) AND
  • at common law – identifies parties, subject matter, consideration, time & nature of performance
  • under UCC – lists quantity of goods (contract enforceable only up to written quantity)
Signature General rule – handwritten signature from, or other mark identifying, party to be charged (eg, letterhead, electronic signature, initials)
  • Merchant exception – between merchants, written confirmation that satisfies statute of frauds as to sender will bind both parties if no written objection within 10 days
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code,

The UCC statute of frauds applies to contracts for the sale of goods valued at $500 or more. To be enforceable, these agreements must be evidenced by a writing that:

  • provides a reasonable basis to believe a contract was formed (eg, the baker's note)
  • lists the quantity of goods sold or the means to determine quantity (eg, 1,000 pounds of flour) and
  • is signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought (here, the supplier) (Choice B).

However, the UCC relaxes the signature requirement in agreements between merchants—ie, regular dealers of the goods involved in the transaction. Under the merchant exception, a written confirmation need only be signed by one merchant and sent to the other merchant. If the recipient has reason to know the confirmation's contents and does not object within 10 days, then it is enforceable against both merchants.

Here, the baker and the supplier are both merchants—regular dealers in flour. The baker's signed note was a sufficient writing because it confirmed that a contract was formed and listed the quantity of goods sold. Additionally, the supplier had reason to know the contents of the note (received and read it) and did not object within 10 days. Therefore, the contract was enforceable against both parties.

(Choice A) Although the parties did not agree to a definitive price term, they did agree to determine the final price at delivery. And even if they are unable to do so, the contract is enforceable since UCC gap-fillers will supply the price term at the time of delivery.

(Choice D) An oral agreement is unenforceable when, as here, it is subject to the statute of frauds. However, the parties' oral agreement was memorialized in a written confirmation that satisfied the merchant exception to this statute and can therefore be enforced.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the merchant exception to the UCC statute of frauds, a confirmation signed and sent by one merchant to another binds both parties if the recipient has reason to know its contents and does not object within 10 days.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-201 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (describing the UCC statute of frauds).
  • U.C.C. § 2-305(1)(b) (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (describing open price terms).
questions.zh-question:
一位商业面包师和一位原料供应商口头约定，面包师将以每磅50至75美分的价格向供应商购买1000磅面粉。双方同意在交货时确定最终价格。供应商承诺在两周内交货。

当天晚些时候，面包师向供应商发送了一份签名的便条，提醒供应商他们协议的条款，包括面粉的数量。供应商收到了这张便条，阅读后未采取任何进一步行动。当供应商未能交付面粉时，面包师以违约为由起诉了供应商。

面包师能否对供应商强制执行该合同？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为双方未就明确的价格条款达成一致。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为供应商没有在该便条上签名。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为面包师向供应商发送了一份签名的确认函。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为双方的口头协议是可强制执行的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Types of Contracts Within the Statute of Frauds

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC货物买卖的 法规书面证据要求（statute of frauds） 里，商人确认函例外（merchant confirmation exception） 能不能让卖方也被绑定。

三秒认题路径：

货物买卖 → 金额超 500 → 书面确认 → 商人间例外 → 能起诉

核心法律规则

UCC法规书面证据（UCC statute of frauds） 适用于价值 500 美元以上的货物买卖，考场意思：没有合格书面材料，口头合同通常先卡住不能直接执行。这个书面要能看出合同确实存在，并写明数量；quantity 最关键，因为 UCC 至少要让数量可识别。

商人确认函（merchant confirmation） 是专门的放宽规则：两边都是商人时，只要一方发出、另一方收到并有理由知道内容，且 10 天内不书面反对，这份确认就能把双方都绑住，考场意思：signed by one merchant 也可能够用，不需要双方都签。

核心判例： 这里锁定的是 UCC 2-201 的商人确认函规则；本题不靠价格条款，而靠“收到后 10 天不反对”把合同拉回可执行。

另外，价格没定死不救题干，UCC 允许 gap-fillers 补价格；所以“先说以后再定价”不等于合同死掉。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 货物买卖（sale of goods），而且金额超过 500？
是进入 UCC § 2-201。
再问：有没有一份能证明合同成立的书面材料，并写了数量？
有继续看签名和商人关系。
最后问：双方是不是商人，且收件人读了确认函后 10 天没反对？
是 第三关卡死：有效执行（enforceable），连没签的人也被绑住。
别被带偏“价格未定”不是终点，因为 UCC 可补价格；真正决定成败的是 书面确认（written confirmation） 和 10 天不反对（no objection within 10 days）。
结论：选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：双方口头只说了“以后定价”，所以合同还不够确定。
但考试真正问的是：法规书面证据（statute of frauds） 有没有被 商人确认函（merchant confirmation） 补上。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，这题不是在抓“价格是否完美”，而是在抓“收到了确认却没在 10 天内反对”这个致命动作。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里 商业烘焙商和供应商都是商人，而且签字确认函写了数量、对方收到后没在 10 天内反对，所以能把合同对双方都变成可执行。

❌ 法律适用 | 价格条款误判

✕ A: 盯着 definitive price 不放，忘了 UCC 可补价格。

❌ 概念混淆 | 签名对象误判

✕ B: 把“谁签字”看成死规则，忽略了商人间确认函只要一方签、另一方不反对也够。

❌ 事实误判 | 口头合同偷换

✕ D: 只看到 oral agreement，没看到后面已经被书面确认补救。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 UCC 货物买卖，再看商人确认函和 10 天无异议，别被“价格未定”带偏。

考场速记

记住这句：两边都是商人 + 一方签字确认 + 对方收到不反对 10 天，就可能把本来口头的货物合同变成可执行。

速记口诀：signed by one merchant，no objection in 10 days，双方都被绑。

reason.en: Establishes a contract for the sale of goods for $500 or more with an open price term.
reason.zh: 确立了一项价格不固定且总额达500美元及以上的货物买卖合同。

highlights.text: the baker sent the supplier a signed note reminding the supplier about the terms of their agreement

reason.en: Triggers the merchant exception by sending a signed written confirmation.
reason.zh: 通过发送签字的书面确认书触发商人例外规则。

highlights.text: The supplier received the note, read it, and took no further action

reason.en: Meets the final requirement of the merchant exception, making the agreement enforceable against the supplier.
reason.zh: 满足商人例外规则的最终要件，使该协议对供货商具有约束力。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An insurance company issued an insurance policy to a homeowner. The policy failed to contain certain coverage terms required by a state insurance statute. When the homeowner suffered a loss due to a theft that was within the policy's terms, the insurance company refused to pay, claiming that the policy was unenforceable because it violated the statute.
Will the homeowner likely succeed in an action against the insurance company to recover for the loss?

choices.A: No, because the insurance policy is not a divisible contract.
choices.B: No, because the insurance policy violated the statute.
choices.C: Yes, because the homeowner belongs to the class of persons intended to be protected by the statute.
choices.D: Yes, because the insurance policy will be strictly construed against the insurance company as the drafter.

questions.explanation:
Contracts unenforceable on public-policy grounds

Common examples:

  • Contracts unreasonably restraining trade
  • Contracts discouraging or restraining marriage
  • Contracts for sexual intercourse
  • Contracts for committing a tort
  • Contracts encouraging breach of a fiduciary duty
  • Contracts excusing liability for intentional, knowing, or reckless misconduct

A contract that violates the law is often unenforceable on public-policy grounds. But there is an exception to this rule when the contract violates a law designed to protect the party seeking to enforce the contract. In that case, the contract is enforceable so as to avoid frustrating the public policy behind the statute.

Here, the homeowner's insurance policy violated the state insurance statute by failing to contain certain coverage terms. That statute was intended to protect insureds like the homeowner, and the public policy behind the statute will be frustrated if the insurance company is allowed to escape liability for the homeowner's loss. Therefore, the insurance policy is enforceable, and the homeowner will likely succeed (Choice B).

(Choice A) Some contracts are divisible, meaning that they can easily be separated into legal and illegal parts so that recovery is available on the legal part(s) only. But a contract entered into in violation of a statute need not be divisible for a court to enforce it.

(Choice D) Although contracts are generally construed against the drafter, this rule matters only when there is a dispute involving the interpretation of ambiguous contract language (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

When a contract violates a law that was designed to protect the party seeking to enforce the contract, the contract can be enforced to avoid frustrating the public policy behind the statute.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 178 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when a contract is unenforceable on public policy grounds).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 179 cmt. c (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (when refusal to enforce frustrates public policy).
questions.zh-question:
一家保险公司向一位房主签发了一份保险单。该保单未能包含州保险法规所要求的某些承保条款。当房主因保单条款范围内的盗窃而遭受损失时，保险公司以该保单违反法规为由，主张其不可强制执行，并拒绝赔付。

房主针对保险公司提起的旨在弥补其损失的诉讼，是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该保险单不是一份可分割的合同。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该保险单违反了法规。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为房主属于该法规意图保护的人群类别。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为作为起草方，该保险单的解释将严格遵循不利于保险公司的原则。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Defenses to enforceability - Defenses to Enforcement

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：合同虽然违反了州法，但如果该法本来就是为了保护主张履行的一方，法院反而可能让它继续有效，避免让另一方借违法逃责。

三秒认题路径：

违反州法 → 谁被保护 → 保护守法方 → 不能借法逃责 → 选 C

核心法律规则

一般来说，违反法律的合同会因公共政策（public policy）而不可执行，考场意思：法院不帮你把违法交易变成可收款的工具。

但有一个例外：如果这部法律本来就是为了保护主张履行的那一方，法院可以让合同可执行，考场意思：不能让被保护的人反过来被对方拿“违法”当盾牌。

本题里的保险法就是为了保护被保险人（insured），所以保险公司不能靠自己没写全条款来逃赔。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 179 cmt. c 的思路锁定本题：拒绝履行会反而破坏立法想保护的一方时，合同仍可执行。

思维导图

合同违反州保险法？
先看默认规则： 违法合同通常因公共政策不可执行。
再看例外： 这部法是不是为了保护主张履行的人？
本题卡点：法条是保护 insured，所以不能让保险公司用自己的违法来脱身。
结论： 合同可执行，投保人可追回损失。
对应答案： C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：合同既然违反了 statute，就应该直接无效。

但考试真正问的是：这部 statute 到底是保护谁的；如果是保护投保人，就不能让保险公司拿“我自己违法”当免责理由。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的保险法是为保护被保险人而设，所以保险公司不能靠自己违反该法来逃避赔付，合同仍可执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 可分割性误判

✕ A: 把 divisible 当成本题关键，但这里根本不是分割履行的问题。

❌ 法律适用 | 违法即无效误判

✕ B: 只看到 violated the statute，却漏掉“该法是保护投保人”的例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 解释规则偷换

✕ D: 把 strictly construed 搬来，但题干没有歧义条款要解释。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问“违法条款保护谁”，再决定是直接否定合同，还是为了不让被保护方被反咬而继续执行。

考场速记

记住这句：违法合同不一定不能执行，先看立法目的是不是在保护主张履行的一方；如果是，法院常会让合同继续有效。

question_analysis.skill_tested: applying public policy defense exception

reason.en: Identifies the party as a member of the class the statute is designed to protect.
reason.zh: 将该当事人识别为法律旨在保护的阶层成员。

reason.en: The law that is violated, which establishes the public policy background.
reason.zh: 被违反的法律，确立了公共政策背景。

reason.en: The defense raised by the insurer to escape liability under the policy.
reason.zh: 保险公司为了规避保险单项下责任而提出的抗辩。

reason.en: Suggests divisibility is needed to enforce the contract, which is incorrect.
reason.zh: 暗示需要合同可分才能执行，这是错误的。

reason.en: Applies the general rule that illegal contracts are unenforceable, ignoring the exception.
reason.zh: 适用违法合同不可执行的一般规则，忽略了例外情况。

C.text: class of persons intended to be protected

label.zh: 成文法意图保护的阶层

reason.en: Correctly identifies the exception allowing enforcement for members of the protected class.
reason.zh: 正确地识别了允许受保护阶层成员执行合同的例外规则。

D.text: strictly construed against the insurance company as the drafter

label.zh: 不利于起草人解释原则

reason.en: Irrelevant rule of construction because there is no ambiguity in the policy terms.
reason.zh: 无关的合同解释规则，因为合同条款并无歧义。

highlights.text: failed to contain certain coverage terms required by a state insurance statute

label.zh: 不符合州保险法规要求

reason.en: Triggers the defense of illegality or public policy violation.
reason.zh: 触发违法性或违反公共政策的抗辩。

highlights.text: refused to pay, claiming that the policy was unenforceable because it violated the statute

reason.en: Shows the insurer trying to escape liability based on the policy violating the law.
reason.zh: 显示保险公司试图以保单违法为由规避赔偿责任。

highlights.text: homeowner suffered a loss due to a theft that was within the policy's terms

label.zh: 保单承保范围内的损失

reason.en: Shows the homeowner is seeking to enforce the policy for a loss that it should cover.
reason.zh: 表明房主正就本应承保的损失寻求执行保单。
